title: Real-world before-and-after evaluation of AI support for lung cancer diagnosis at three US lung nodule clinics.
abstract: Background Health systems and payers require evidence that artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support improves care delivery. Integrating AI into lung nodule management pathways may streamline workflows, improve identification and triage of patients with pulmonary nodules, and enable earlier lung cancer diagnosis. Yet real-world evidence of clinical utility remains limited. This study evaluated the impact of implementing commercially available AI software to support the lung nodule and lung cancer care pathway across three US health systems. Materials and methods A real-world before-and-after study compared clinic activity during matched 12.5-month pre-implementation and post-implementation periods at three US lung nodule clinics. Primary outcomes were the number of new patients and the number of patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure. Secondary outcomes were numbers of lung cancers and early-stage (stages I-II) lung cancers, and time from baseline CT to diagnosis. Analyses used Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests, with medians and interquartile ranges (IQRs) reported for continuous measures. Results Across sites, new patients increased from 138 before to 232 after implementation, equivalent to 11.0 to 18.6 patients per month (p = 0.0002), with the median rising from 9 (IQR 7-14) to 16 (IQR 13-21) patients. Monthly patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure increased from 4.9 to 8.0 (p = 0.0085). Monthly cancers increased from 3.0 to 3.8 (p = 0.3242), while monthly early-stage cancers rose from 1.4 to 2.4 (p = 0.125). Median time to diagnosis was 58 days (IQR 33-158) before and 57 days (IQR 27-85) after implementation (p = 0.26), with IQR narrowing from 125 days to 58 days. Conclusion Implementation of the AI-enabled software was associated with significantly increased throughput of lung nodule patients and procedural volume. These results, observed prospectively post-implementation, suggest AI-assisted identification and triage can expand access to timely specialist review.

title: Association between thoracolumbar kyphosis and fracture risk assessment tool in Korean postmenopausal women: A retrospective study.
abstract: Thoracolumbar kyphosis (TLK) has been suggested as a potential risk factor for vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women; however, its association with bone mineral density (BMD), trabecular bone score (TBS), and fracture risk assessment tools, such as the Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX), remain undefined. In this study, we investigated the association between the TLK level and fracture risk in postmenopausal women. We retrospectively analyzed the associations between the thoracolumbar Cobb (TLCobb) angle, baseline compression fractures, BMD, TBS, and volumetric BMD measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and central quantitative computed tomography (cQCT). The study included 251 postmenopausal women (median age, 61 years; interquartile range, 56-69 years) who visited our hospital for health checkups between March 2020 and December 2021. Fracture risk was assessed using FRAX and TBS-adjusted FRAX. Baseline radiography revealed patients with compression fractures (n = 64, 25.498%), in whom the TLCobb angle was significantly higher. The TLCobb angle demonstrated a significant negative correlation with TBS. Baseline compression fractures and higher TLCobb angles were significant predictors of future fragility compression fractures, with a TLCobb angle > 9.4° established as the threshold value. DXA and FRAX had limitations in predicting future progressive or new-onset compression fractures. In conclusion, TLK was found to be associated with densitometric results, particularly TBS, and has predictive value for future compression fracture risk. Baseline compression fractures with higher TLCobb angles are potential predictors of fracture risk in postmenopausal women.

title: Research on precise segmentation model of thyroid nodules based on deep learning.
abstract: Thyroid nodules are a prevalent condition in clinical practice, typically identified via ultrasound imaging with visual assessment by physicians. However, the ambiguous features of malignant nodules, their proximity to surrounding tissues, image noise, and unclear boundaries can lead to variability in diagnostic outcomes among different practitioners. In this study, we initially employed nine established models to segment ultrasound images from two publicly available datasets, TN3K and DDTI. Evaluation metrics including IoU, F1-score, accuracy (Acc), specificity (Spec), and precision (Pre) were utilized to assess the segmentation performance of these models. The experimental results indicate that, given the current data scale, the overall segmentation performance of each model is relatively low. Analysis suggests this is primarily due to the limited number of samples in the medical imaging dataset. During training, the model struggles to fully learn the discriminative features of the lesion area. Particularly during the encoder's down-sampling stage, the feature expression ability is constrained, affecting the model's ability to accurately recognize lesion locations. To address this, we enhanced the classic model by incorporating the Residual Network ResNet34, constructing a new thyroid nodule segmentation model. The improved model demonstrated enhanced segmentation performance, with most IoU values on the TN3K dataset exceeding 0.8. However, models trained on the DDTI dataset rarely achieved high performance. Further analysis attributes this performance disparity to differences in the number of training samples. To further enhance model performance, we initialized the improved model with pre-trained ResNet34 weights from the ImageNet dataset, resulting in significant performance improvements. Notably, Res34-PAN performed best across both datasets. On the DDTI dataset, the model achieved an IoU of 0.8778, an F1-score of 0.9349, an accuracy of 0.9872, a specificity of 0.9928, and a precision of 0.9342. To further validate the model design's rationale, we conducted a systematic ablation experiment. We selected commonly used network structures for encoders and used them as the encoders for nine segmentation models, comparing performance with and without the ImageNet pre-trained weights. The results further confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed method in the thyroid nodule segmentation task.

title: Comparative evaluation of YOLO models for retained root fragment detection.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and comparatively evaluate four YOLO nano-scale one-stage object detectors-YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLO11n, and YOLO12n-for the automated detection of retained root fragments in dental radiographic images, under identical preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocols. Methods A curated dataset was organized in the YOLO format and evaluated using a nested 5-fold cross-validation strategy to prevent data leakage. An ablation study was additionally conducted to validate the combined bilateral filtering and histogram equalization (BF + HE) preprocessing pipeline. Four YOLO models were fine-tuned from official pretrained weights over 200 epochs. Detection performance was assessed at both the epoch level and the decision-threshold level, reporting the unbiased mean and standard deviation across the independent test folds for precision, sensitivity, F1 score, mean average precision (mAP), and false positives per image (FP/image). Results In the primary multi-model benchmark, YOLO12n achieved the highest overall detection performance across the held-out test folds, yielding a mean best-epoch F1 score of 0.885 ± 0.007, mAP@0.5 of 0.919 ± 0.021, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.447 ± 0.025 (reaching an optimal-threshold F1 score of 0.888 ± 0.016 with 0.346 ± 0.052 FP/image). YOLO11n followed closely as the second-best performing architecture (F1 = 0.874 ± 0.012, mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.445 ± 0.019). Furthermore, the preprocessing ablation study confirmed that the hybrid BF + HE pipeline improved detection performance over raw radiographs, elevating YOLO12n's F1 score from 0.856 ± 0.013 to 0.888 ± 0.016 and mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.438 ± 0.011 to 0.461 ± 0.008. All models demonstrated stable convergence behavior. Conclusions Modern YOLO architectures, particularly YOLO12n and YOLO11n, demonstrate technical efficacy for automated RRF localization. The observed performance advantages of YOLO12n are associated with its overall architectural refinements, though dedicated modular ablation studies are warranted to isolate the exact contribution of individual attention mechanisms. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of lightweight one-stage object detectors for identifying retained root fragments in dental panoramic radiographs, serving as a baseline for future prospective clinical evaluations.

title: ReViT-RF: A hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with a Radiomic Feature Fusion framework for lung tumor classification and TNM-based stage prediction using CT images.
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape, size, texture, and spatial descriptors, are fused with deep features to provide clinically meaningful information for accurate TNM component prediction. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, with data augmentation applied only to the training set to prevent information leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97.62% for benign-malignant classification, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Moreover, independent prediction of TNM components provides detailed stage-related information rather than relying on a single aggregated stage label, enabling more precise tumor assessment and clinical decision support. Furthermore, explainability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) identifies the critical tumor regions contributing to model predictions, improving interpretability and enhancing clinician confidence. Overall, by combining hybrid deep feature extraction, radiomic feature fusion, component-wise TNM stage prediction, and explainable AI analysis, the proposed ReViT-RF framework provides a reliable, comprehensive, and clinically interpretable solution for automated lung tumor analysis.

title: Multi-feature Response Attention Network for kidney stone detection and measurement of stone size in ultrasound images.
abstract: Kidney stones are hard deposits formed in the urinary tract due to excess waste and low fluid intake, causing severe abdominal pain. Ultrasound-based kidney stone detection involves identifying and locating stones in the kidneys using high-frequency sound waves to visualize renal structures. Measuring stone size is crucial for early treatment and preventing infection. However, detection is challenging because ultrasound images suffer from noise, lower contrast, and variable quality. To overcome these limitations, the Multi-feature Response Attention Network (MFRANet) is proposed to detect kidney stones. Initially, the input image is allowed for image denoising and edge preservation using Windowed Variation Kernel Wiener Filter (WV-KWF). Further, the kidney region is segmented by the Fuzzy Clustering algorithm with Variable Multi-pixel Fitting spatial information (FCM-VMF). Moreover, descriptor computation is processed by rotated Binary Robust Independent Elementary Feature (rBRIEF) with Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). Afterwards, the kidney stone is detected using MFRANet, wherein MFRANet is designed by combining Multi-feature Multi-Attention Network (MFMANet), along with Group Response Attention Network (GRA-Net). Next, the detected stone is segmented using Optimized DA-TransUNet (O-DAT), and lastly, the kidney stone size is measured. Performance of the proposed MFRANet is assessed with Accuracy, F1-score, Precision, and True Positive Rate (TPR) which achieved superior values of 96.64%, 96.65%, 97.44%, 95.88% Response Attention Network, Multi-feature Multi-Attention Network, Optimized DA-TransUNet.

title: Prospective multicenter study on patient-related outcomes of orbital floor reconstruction using ultrahigh-molecular-weight polyethylene.
abstract: This prospective, multicenter clinical study evaluated patient-reported outcomes, functional recovery, and quality of life following orbital floor reconstruction using ultra-high-molecular-weight-polyethylene (UHMWPE) implants. The study emphasized both subjective recovery and the clinical performance of the implant material. Between June 2022 and July 2023, 46 adult patients (≥ 18 years of age) with radiologically confirmed orbital floor fractures requiring surgical reconstruction were enrolled and completed the full follow-up protocol. Surgical reconstruction was performed according to standardized procedures using UHMWPE implants. Pre- and postoperative CT or CBCT imaging was obtained when clinically indicated; radiological outcomes of this cohort have been reported separately. Pre- and postoperative evaluations included an assessment of pain, swelling, ocular motility, diplopia, sensory function, foreign body sensation, overall satisfaction and orbital volume, which was measured using three-dimensional imaging. Intraoperative parameters were also recorded. Patient-reported outcomes were collected through validated questionnaires and visual analogue scales, repeated at each visit, follow-up examinations were performed approximately one day, ten weeks, six months, and twelve months after surgery. Overall, clinical and patient-reported outcomes improved over the follow-up period. Pain intensity declined markedly within the first week after surgery and remained consistently low thereafter. Swelling, numbness, and the sensation of a foreign body gradually subsided, with almost complete resolution after one year. Furthermore, imaging confirmed stable anatomical reconstruction without implant displacement or volume loss. In general patient satisfaction increased steadily throughout the observation period, reaching near-maximal levels after twelve months. No cases of infection, inflammatory reaction or implant-related complication were recorded. In this prospective cohort, orbital floor reconstruction using UHMWPE was associated with favorable functional, aesthetic and patient-reported recovery over 12 months. These findings support the value of incorporating patient-centered outcomes into the assessment of recovery after orbital trauma, while comparative effectiveness and long-term safety require further controlled studies.

title: RCTE: A multi-class object detection framework for dental panoramic radiographs.
abstract: Background Dental panoramic radiographs play an important role in oral disease screening, computer-aided diagnosis, and clinical treatment planning. However, accurate multi-class detection remains challenging due to small lesion sizes, ambiguous anatomical boundaries, insufficient multi-scale feature representation, and missed detections of complex dental structures. Objective This study aims to develop an accurate and efficient multi-class object detection framework for dental panoramic radiographs to improve the detection performance of small lesions, weak-boundary structures, and complex anatomical targets. Methods A novel re-parameterized cross-scale attention-enhanced framework, named RCTE, was proposed based on the YOLOv8n detector. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components: a Cross-Scale Channel Transformer (CSCT) module for cross-scale contextual interaction among P3, P4, and P5 features, a RepNCSPELAN4-based Re-parameterized Feature Pyramid Fusion (RPF) structure for enhancing multi-scale feature aggregation, and a Multi-Scale EMA (MS-EMA) mechanism for feature recalibration before the detection head. Experiments were conducted on a publicly available dental panoramic radiograph dataset containing 11 categories of dental structures and lesions. Model performance was evaluated using Precision, Recall, F1-score, mAP50, mAP75, and mAP50-95. Results Compared with the original YOLOv8n baseline, RCTE improved mAP50, mAP75, mAP50-95, and Recall by 2.55, 3.88, 2.40, and 5.10 percentage points, respectively. The proposed framework achieved better detection completeness and localization accuracy compared with other YOLO-based detectors. Furthermore, RCTE maintained real-time inference capability, demonstrating a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Conclusion The proposed RCTE framework effectively improves multi-class object detection performance in dental panoramic radiographs by enhancing cross-scale feature interaction, multi-scale feature fusion, and detection feature recalibration. This method provides a potential solution for computer-aided dental image analysis.

title: Efficacy evaluation of the cervical posterior "keyhole technique" in the treatment of cervical radiculopathy: A retrospective case series.
abstract: Study design Retrospective clinical study. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression for cervical radiculopathy and to investigate the correlation between decompression parameters and clinical outcomes. Summary of background data Cervical radiculopathy traditionally requires anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) or open posterior decompression. Although ACDF is the gold standard, it is associated with adjacent segment degeneration and implant-related complications. Minimally invasive posterior keyhole techniques aim to reduce surgical trauma; however, the optimal extent of decompression required for symptomatic relief remains unclear. Methods Forty patients with single-level cervical radiculopathy treated via unilateral endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression (strictly limited to targeted foraminotomy and partial medial facetectomy) (2021-2024) were reviewed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Neck Disability Index (NDI) preoperatively, at discharge, and at 6 months postoperatively. Decompression parameters were quantified via postoperative CT. Statistical analysis included paired t-tests and Pearson correlation. Results All 40 procedures were successful. Specifically, 25 patients underwent isolated foraminotomy, and 15 received foraminotomy combined with discectomy, without any progression to interlaminar decompression or laminectomy. The mean operative time was 70.4 ± 24.7 minutes, and the mean blood loss was 11.7 ± 10.9 ml. Significant improvements in clinical scores were observed at all postoperative time points (P < 0.05). Statistical analysis revealed that neither the concurrent execution of a discectomy nor the diameter of the bony decompression window was significantly associated with the degree of postoperative symptom improvement. Conclusions This study demonstrates that endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression is a safe and feasible technique that provides favorable short-term clinical outcomes with minimal surgical trauma. The findings strongly suggest that clinical efficacy depends on targeted neural decompression (determined by intraoperative nerve root mobility) rather than the maximal removal of disc tissue or extensive laminoforaminotomy.

title: COlour vision assessment for the Detection of Early diabetic Retinopathy (CODER): A study protocol.
abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains one of the leading causes of preventable vision loss. However, high-contrast visual acuity, which is routinely used in the clinic, is often preserved during the early stages of the disease, limiting its usefulness in detecting early functional deficits. Colour vision is a sensitive marker for detecting these early retinal changes. This study aims to investigate whether the Colour Assessment and Diagnosis (CAD) test, a quantitative measure of chromatic sensitivity, can serve as a functional biomarker for the early detection of DR and can reflect the severity of the disease. Methods and analysis This prospective observational study will be conducted at the L V Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad, India. Adults aged 18 years and above will be recruited into three groups: healthy controls, individuals with diabetes without diabetic retinopathy, and individuals with diabetic retinopathy. All participants will undergo a comprehensive ophthalmic examination, colour vision testing, fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), and systemic metabolic investigations, including glycaemic, renal, and lipid profiles. The primary outcome measures are the Red-Green (RG) and Yellow-Blue (YB) Colour thresholds. Secondary outcome measures include retinal structural parameters and vascular parameters, such as retinal thickness, vessel density, and perfusion density. Systemic metabolic parameters, including HbA1c, random blood glucose, renal function, and lipid profile, will be evaluated as independent variables. Statistical analyses will include correlation, multiple regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the CAD test in the detection of early DR. Conclusion The current study is expected to provide evidence whether quantitative colour vision assessment can act as a functional marker of early retinal changes in diabetes and diabetic retinopathy.

title: Dynamic assessment of renal resistive index using point-of-care ultrasonography for early detection of sepsis-induced acute kidney injury: A multicenter clinical trial protocol.
abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and serious complication of sepsis, significantly increasing both mortality risk and healthcare costs. Early prediction and diagnosis of sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI) remain challenging due to the delayed detection of existing renal injury markers. Although research suggests that the Renal Resistive Index (RRI) shows promise for earlier prediction of AKI, large-scale, multicenter clinical studies to support this are currently lacking. Methods This multicenter, open-label, prospective observational cohort study enrolled 238 patients who were diagnosed with sepsis according to the Sepsis 3.0 criteria. The Renal Resistive Index (RRI) was measured using bedside ultrasound within 2 hours of diagnosis and subsequently every 8 hours during their individualized standard treatment. Concurrently, blood samples were collected to quantify creatinine and cystatin C, and urine samples were obtained to detect kidney injury markers, including TIMP-2/IGFBP-7. The primary endpoint is to determine the threshold and accuracy of the Renal Resistive Index in predicting sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). Secondary endpoints include examining the dynamic trend of the RRI, assessing the RRI's predictive value for 28-day mortality in sepsis, and evaluating the correlation between the RRI and creatinine, cystatin C, and urinary TIMP-2/IGFBP-7 levels. Discussion This study assesses the accuracy and feasibility of using bedside ultrasonography to monitor the Renal Resistive Index (RRI) for the early detection of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). Early identification of SA-AKI is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in sepsis, making this approach highly relevant for timely intervention. Ethics and dissemination This study received ethical approval from the Ethics Committee of the initiator's institution. Study results will be initially reported to the collaborating investigators. Following review and consensus by the Trial Steering Committee, the research report will be drafted by the initiating investigator and disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and presentations at scientific conferences. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400082420), Registered on March 28, 2024.

title: Vigorous physical activity and physical function are strongly associated with better health in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the impact of physical function and level of physical activity on health status and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA). Methods In total, 141 patients with long-standing r-axSpA were included in this cross-sectional cohort study. Assessments included physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI)), spinal mobility (modified Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI)), muscle function for leg strength (Timed Stands Test (TST)) and handgrip force (Grippit), amount of self-reported physical activity (vigorous physical activity, moderate physical activity, sedentary behavior), health status by ASAS Health Index (ASAS HI) and HRQoL with Short Form Survey Instrument 36-Item. Multivariable linear regression was used to analyze associations between health status, HRQoL, physical activity, muscle function, and physical function. Results The mean (SD) age was 60 (12) years, diagnosis duration was 25 (10) years, and 57% were male. Physical function and vigorous physical activity were the strongest determinants of health status and HRQoL. The models explained approximately 50% of the variation in ASAS HI and the physical aspects of HRQoL and 21% of the mental aspects of HRQoL. Participants displayed good health status (62%) by ASAS HI ≤ 5, reached the recommended level of health-enhancing physical activity (77%), had normal muscle function (TST 82% and Grippit 91%), and demonstrated physical function (55%), and spinal mobility (45%) within reference values. Conclusion This study highlights the importance of regular vigorous physical activity in older individuals living with long-standing r-axSpA since it was strongly associated with health status and HRQoL.

title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices. Aims The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI. Methods Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance. Results Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions. Conclusion The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.

title: ScaffoldForge: Bioinspired generative design of 3D-printed bone scaffolds via conditional diffusion for large segmental bone defect reconstruction.
abstract: We present ScaffoldForge, a 3D conditional diffusion framework for the generative design of bone scaffolds. ScaffoldForge maps a set of standardized trabecular descriptors (bone volume fraction BV/TV, trabecular thickness Tb.Th, trabecular spacing Tb.Sp, trabecular number Tb.N, connectivity density Conn.D, structure model index SMI, degree of anisotropy DA, and permeability k) to a 3D scaffold architecture in a single forward pass. A multi-objective conditioning mechanism couples these descriptors through adaptive instance normalization, and a physics-constrained loss adds empirical penalties for stiffness, manufacturing feasibility, and perfusion, evaluated on the denoiser's reconstruction of the clean scaffold so that the penalties carry gradient. To address the scarcity of paired geometry-property data, we describe a procedural pipeline whose generated scaffolds reproduce the morphometric distributions of real micro-CT references. In an in silico evaluation on three benchmark datasets, ScaffoldForge attains an estimated 56.6 MPa compressive strength (8.2% over topology optimization; paired t-test, p = 0.043, n = 5 seeds) and reduces design-time cost from 8,400-12 seconds per design, a 700× speedup. Generated structures are diverse rather than memorized, and morphometric accuracy holds across all seven shape descriptors. Three analyses probe the reliability of these results given the small training corpus. Equivalence testing replaces the earlier argument from non-significant difference tests: the procedural and real descriptor distributions are equivalent at a medium margin of 0.5 standard deviations for all seven descriptors, but the 50 available real reference volumes cannot establish equivalence at a strict 0.3-standard-deviation margin for five of them. A classifier two-sample test shows that generated scaffolds retain a measurable but shrinking signature of the procedural generator. Enlarging the corpus from 250 to 2,050 scaffolds leaves in-distribution accuracy nearly unchanged while reducing the cross-dataset descriptor error on unseen anatomy from 0.079 to 0.058, which localizes the cost of the small corpus in generalization rather than in fit. We further illustrate a CT-to-scaffold pipeline for personalized generation. All results are computational; physical, biological, manufacturing, and regulatory validation remain future work.

title: Predicting lymph node metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer using clinical and PET/CT-derived morphological features: An interpretable machine-learning study.
abstract: Background Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is crucial for staging and treatment planning. This study aimed to establish a standardized machine learning workflow based on routinely available clinical, serological, and PET/CT-derived parameters to enhance preoperative LNM risk stratification. Methods This retrospective study included 255 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC, all of whom underwent systematic lymph-node dissection. Patients were randomly divided, with stratification by pathological lymph-node status, into a training cohort (n = 178) and an internal held-out test test cohort (n = 77). Candidate predictors were screened using univariable and multivariable logistic regression in the training cohort. Six machine-learning algorithms were trained and optimized using repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. After model development was completed, all six models were applied without modification to the test cohort. Test-set AUCs were compared using paired DeLong tests with Holm correction. The primary model was further evaluated for calibration, clinical utility, and feature contribution using SHAP. A conventional multivariable logistic regression model using the same four predictors was added as a simple reference model, and its discrimination and calibration were compared with those of XGBoost. Results Central tumor location, elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, elevated squamous cell carcinoma antigen, and solid nodule status were retained as predictors; none of the quantitative PET metabolic parameters remained independently associated with LNM. XGBoost achieved the highest cross-validated AUC among the six candidate machine-learning algorithms in the training cohort (0.735; 95% CI, 0.653-0.813) and was therefore designated the primary model. In the internal held-out test cohort, XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.747 (95% CI, 0.631-0.846). The conventional logistic regression reference model achieved a test AUC of 0.733 (95% CI, 0.612-0.841), with no significant difference from XGBoost (DeLong P = 0.301). Its Brier score was 0.152, compared with 0.198 for XGBoost. Conclusion XGBoost model showed moderate discrimination and a high negative predictive value for pathological LNM in NSCLC. However, its limited positive predictive value and the absence of significant differences among the candidate algorithms support cautious interpretation. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Study on the molecular mechanism of chlorotoxin from Buthus martensii Karsch in the inhibition of glioma angiogenesis.
abstract: Background Glioma is a highly malignant intracranial tumor with dismal prognosis. Tumor angiogenesis critically drives glioma growth and invasion, making vascular endothelial cells a promising therapeutic target. Buthus martensii Karsch chlorotoxin (BmK CT) presents favorable antitumor properties, whereas its regulatory role in glioma angiogenesis and the specific mechanism remain poorly defined. Aim To investigate the regulatory role of BmK CT in glioma angiogenesis and the underlying mechanism. Methods HUVECs were cultured alone or exposed to glioma conditioned medium prepared from primary glioma cells. Functional assays were performed to assess the impacts of BmK CT on endothelial proliferation, migration and tube formation. Quantitative proteomics and bioinformatics analysis were applied to screen differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and explore underlying mechanisms. Results BmK CT significantly inhibited the proliferation of HUVEC cells and reduced their migration and tube formation abilities. BmK CT reversed the promoting effect of primary glioma cells on the migration of HUVEC cells. Proteomics identified multiple DEPs. Enrichment analysis suggested that BmK CT exerts an anti-glioma angiogenesis effect through a multi-target mechanism by inhibiting pro-angiogenic pathways, blocking energy metabolism, and regulating the inflammatory microenvironment. Furthermore, expression pattern clustering analysis revealed six DEPs expression patterns. Parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) analysis supported nine candidate proteins (THBS1, THBS4, COMP, F2, A2M, C3, RIGI, EZR, and ITGA6) associated with glioma angiogenesis. Conclusion: This study demonstrated in vitro that BmK CT inhibits endothelial angiogenic behaviors relevant to glioma progression and modulates the tumor microenvironment, and identified nine candidate DEPs, providing a theoretical basis for future molecular targeted therapy strategies for glioma.

To investigate the regulatory role of BmK CT in glioma angiogenesis and the underlying mechanism.

Methods

HUVECs were cultured alone or exposed to glioma conditioned medium prepared from primary glioma cells. Functional assays were performed to assess the impacts of BmK CT on endothelial proliferation, migration and tube formation. Quantitative proteomics and bioinformatics analysis were applied to screen differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and explore underlying mechanisms.

Results

BmK CT significantly inhibited the proliferation of HUVEC cells and reduced their migration and tube formation abilities. BmK CT reversed the promoting effect of primary glioma cells on the migration of HUVEC cells. Proteomics identified multiple DEPs. Enrichment analysis suggested that BmK CT exerts an anti-glioma angiogenesis effect through a multi-target mechanism by inhibiting pro-angiogenic pathways, blocking energy metabolism, and regulating the inflammatory microenvironment. Furthermore, expression pattern clustering analysis revealed six DEPs expression patterns. Parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) analysis supported nine candidate proteins (THBS1, THBS4, COMP, F2, A2M, C3, RIGI, EZR, and ITGA6) associated with glioma angiogenesis. Conclusion: This study demonstrated in vitro that BmK CT inhibits endothelial angiogenic behaviors relevant to glioma progression and modulates the tumor microenvironment, and identified nine candidate DEPs, providing a theoretical basis for future molecular targeted therapy strategies for glioma.

title: Investigating the potential association between the continuous-time random-walk MR diffusion model and lymph node metastasis and vascular invasion in patients with rectal cancer: A preliminary exploratory study.
abstract: Objectives To explore, as a preliminary study, the quantitative parameters of single-index and continuous-time random-walk (CTRW) magnetic resonance (MR) diffusion models and their association with lymph node metastasis, vascular invasion, and some prognostic factors in patients with rectal cancer. Methods This retrospective, exploratory study included a total of 43 patients who were pathologically diagnosed with rectal cancer and underwent preoperative MRI between February 2022 and November 2023. The data were fitted using the single-index and CTRW diffusion models to derive ADC, Dm, α, and β parameters. Differences in quantitative diffusion parameters were assessed for lymph node metastasis, vascular invasion, and p53 status using t-tests and rank-sum tests. The associations of quantitative diffusion parameters with lymph node metastasis and vascular invasion were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results Lymph node metastasis was positive in 25 patients and negative in 18 patients; vascular invasion was positive in 30 patients and negative in 13 patients. In this initial investigation, the Dm and β values derived from the CTRW model showed a certain association with lymph node metastasis (AUCs of 0.76 and 0.76, respectively). Regarding vascular invasion, only the Dm value showed a certain association (AUC of 0.76), while the β value did not demonstrate a significant association after adjustment.The combination of Dm and β demonstrated stronger associations, with AUCs of 0.83 and 0.83, respectively. Conclusion In this exploratory study, the diffusion parameters derived from the CTRW model may be associated with lymph node metastasis and vascular invasion in rectal cancer, but this requires external validation.

title: Association between coronary artery calcium score and myocardial ischemia assessed by stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Background Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring effectively stratifies cardiovascular risk, and stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) accurately detects myocardial ischemia. We aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with myocardial ischemia on CMR in patients with CAC, and to assess the clinical impact of myocardial ischemia following CMR. Methods This study included 215 patients aged ≥18 years who underwent CAC scoring for risk stratification, followed by stress CMR between 2013 and 2026. The prevalence and predictors of myocardial ischemia were investigated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the association between CAC scores and myocardial ischemia. Additionally, subsequent clinical management following CMR was determined. Results The mean age was 69.3 ± 9.1 years (60.9% male). The average 10-year PREVENT risk score was 18.6 ± 8.7%. Overall, myocardial ischemia was present in 26.0% of patients (56/215): 17.1% in the CAC 300-999 Agatston units (AU) group (14/82) and 41.6% in the CAC ≥ 1,000 AU group (42/101). CAC score was the only independent predictor of myocardial ischemia (adjusted OR 1.07, 95%CI 1.03 - 1.10; p < 0.001 per 100 AU). Across clinical risk score categories and diabetes status, CAC score was consistently associated with myocardial ischemia, with no significant interactions observed (all p for interaction >0.05).The number of ischemic segments increased with increasing CAC scores (p < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an optimal cutoff threshold of CAC ≥ 1,093 AU for detecting myocardial ischemia (AUC 0.75, p < 0.001). The clinical impact of stress CMR included medication changes in 37.2% of patients, while 18.1% underwent invasive procedures. Conclusions In patients with CAC scores undergoing stress CMR, the prevalence of myocardial ischemia was approximately one-fourth and was associated with higher CAC scores. Stress CMR may influence clinical management in this population. Larger or prospective studies validating these findings and evaluating prognosis are warranted.

title: Integrating Non-Invasive Liver Assessment into Screening Colonoscopy: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Introduction Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits. Methods This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds. Results Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds. Discussion Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

title: Case of Appendiceal Goblet Cell Adenocarcinoma With Gastric Metastasis.
abstract: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma (GCA) is a rare appendiceal neoplasm that typically metastasizes to the peritoneum and pelvic organs, with no reported gastric involvement. We report a 72-year-old man with multiple comorbidities presenting with recurrent small bowel obstruction. Imaging revealed a cecal and a gastric mass; colonoscopy confirmed poorly differentiated right-sided adenocarcinoma. Surgical resection with intraoperative biopsies identified high-grade appendiceal GCA infiltrating the cecum, mesentery, and gastric wall. Immunohistochemical staining showed cytokeratin 7 negativity and cytokeratin 20 positivity, suggesting an appendiceal origin. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of the gastric lesion confirmed gastric metastasis, demonstrating identical morphology and immunoprofile, thus expanding the metastatic spectrum of GCA.

title: When Imaging is Negative: Endoscopic Diagnosis of a Secondary Aortoduodenal Fistula.
abstract: Aortoenteric fistula is a life-threatening aortic graft complication with a narrow opportunity for treatment. We present a patient with aortobifemoral bypass who developed recurrent anemia and melena. Despite previous upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, computed tomography angiogram, and tagged red blood cell scan, his symptoms were persistent. Capsule endoscopy showed blood in the duodenum. Push enteroscopy revealed graft erosion in the duodenum, confirming aortoduodenal fistula. He underwent aortobifemoral graft excision, and resection of the third portion of the duodenum with end-to-side duodenojejunostomy, highlighting the importance of endoscopy in timely diagnosis of aortoenteric fistulae.

title: Whipple Disease: A Two-Decade Multisystem Masquerade Preceding Gastrointestinal Presentation.
abstract: Whipple disease is a rare multisystem infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei that can present with extraintestinal manifestations preceding gastrointestinal symptoms by years. We report an unusually prolonged course in a patient with nearly 2 decades of treatment-refractory seronegative inflammatory polyarthritis who later developed gastrointestinal symptoms. Although initial upper endoscopy with biopsies was nondiagnostic, repeat evaluation following symptom progression demonstrated small bowel involvement, with diagnosis established by periodic acid-Schiff staining and polymerase chain reaction of small bowel biopsies. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of Whipple disease and the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion in longstanding refractory symptoms and multisystem involvement.

title: Accuracy of Augmented Reality-Guided Angular Trajectories in Spine Surgery: A Cadaveric Study Comparing 2D-3D vs Intraoperative Computed Tomography Registration.
abstract: Background Augmented reality (AR) navigation has demonstrated accuracy for pedicle screw placement but has not been well studied for angular trajectories required to access disc spaces and sacroiliac joints (SIJs). This study evaluated the accuracy of AR-guided angular trajectories comparing 2 registration methods: intraoperative 3D computed tomography (CT)-based registration and 2D-3D registration using intraoperative radiographs matched to preoperative CT imaging. Methods In this prospective cadaveric study, 4 experienced spine surgeons performed 67 AR-navigated angular trajectories targeting thoracic, lumbar, and SIJ anatomy across 4 human cadavers. Jamshidi tools were used to simulate angular navigation. Trajectories were planned using either intraoperative CT registration or 2D-3D registration. Absolute stereotactic accuracy was assessed by comparing postoperative CT trajectories to the system's virtual trajectories. Angular deviations were measured in axial and sagittal planes with a predefined success criterion of a 99% upper confidence bound ≤3.0°. Results All trajectories, including 32 medial, 31 lateral, and 4 intracanal (trajectories directed into the spinal canal to simulate access pathways for decompression or discal approaches), met predefined accuracy criteria for both methods. The 99% upper bounds of angular error were 1.65° (axial) and 1.54° (sagittal) for intraoperative registration and 1.78° (axial) and 1.75° (sagittal) for 2D-3D registration. Mean angular errors in both planes remained below 3.0°. Cadavers had a mean age of 72.5 years and a mean body mass index of 22.2. Conclusion AR-guided navigation enables accurate angular trajectory guidance for disc space and SIJ targeting. Comparable accuracy between intraoperative CT and 2D-3D registration suggests that 2D-3D AR workflows may reduce radiation exposure and operative time while maintaining precision. Clinical relevance AR navigation may improve surgical workflow by providing real-time 3D visualization while reducing reliance on intraoperative CT, potentially decreasing radiation exposure and operative time without compromising accuracy in complex spine procedures. Level of evidence Level 5 (cadaveric study).

title: L5 Corpectomy in a 12-Year-Old Owing to Rosai-Dorfman Disease: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically presenting with massive, painless lymphadenopathy or subcutaneous masses. Extranodal involvement, particularly in the spine, is exceedingly rare and poses significant diagnostic and management challenges. Lumbar spinal RDD with vertebral collapse and neurological compromise is almost unheard of in the pediatric population, with no prior reports of surgical intervention requiring L5 corpectomy and circumferential fusion in an adolescent. Case description We present a case of a 12-year-old girl with a 6-month history of worsening lower back pain unresponsive to conservative treatment. Imaging revealed collapse of the L5 vertebral body and a destructive, enhancing lesion encasing the neural elements, leading to severe canal and foraminal stenosis. Computed tomography-guided biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of RDD. A multidisciplinary surgical team implemented a 2-stage circumferential surgical plan. Stage 1 involved posterior decompression and posterior instrumentation from L3 to the pelvis using S2AI screws. A silastic barrier was placed to protect neural elements. Stage 2, performed via an anterior approach with vascular surgery assistance, involved complete corpectomy of L5 and reconstruction with an expandable cage spanning L4 to S1. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient remained neurologically intact. At 1-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated solid anterior and posterior fusion, maintained spinal alignment, and had returned to full activity. Conclusion This is the first reported case of pediatric RDD requiring an L5 corpectomy with circumferential spinal fusion. The case underscores the importance of early tissue diagnosis, individualized surgical planning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Recognition of RDD as a potential etiology for pediatric spinal lesions is critical, particularly when imaging mimics malignancy. Our successful outcome supports the use of staged, tailored surgical approaches in managing rare spinal pathologies in children.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of preoperative magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography in delineating biliary anatomy in live liver donors: An ambispective observational study.
abstract: Backgrounds/aims Accurate preoperative delineation of biliary anatomy is essential for living donor liver transplantation (LDLT), as unrecognised variants contribute to biliary complications. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) for characterising biliary anatomy in live donors, using intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) as the reference standard. Methods An ambispective observational study included 89 live liver donors (65 retrospective, 24 prospective) at a tertiary LDLT centre. Biliary anatomy was classified on MRCP and IOC using the Huang classification. Variant anatomy (Huang types A2-A5) was defined as the positive test condition and standard anatomy (A1) as the negative condition. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and Cohen's kappa. Results The cohort comprised 58 females (65.2%) and 31 males (34.8%), with a mean age of 34.34 ± 9.53 years. Huang type A1 was most common on MRCP (65.2%) and IOC (59.6%), while variants (A2-A5) were detected in 34.8% and 40.4%, respectively. Against IOC, MRCP showed 77.78% sensitivity (95% CI, 61.92%-88.28%), 94.34% specificity (95% CI, 84.63%-98.06%), 90.32% positive predictive value (95% CI, 75.10%-96.65%), 86.21% negative predictive value (95% CI, 75.07%-92.84%), and 87.64% overall accuracy, with substantial agreement (κ = 0.737, p < 0.001). Conclusions MRCP is highly specific for preoperative biliary mapping in LDLT donors but has limited sensitivity for variants, supporting routine IOC before ductal transection.

Against IOC, MRCP showed 77.78% sensitivity (95% CI, 61.92%-88.28%), 94.34% specificity (95% CI, 84.63%-98.06%), 90.32% positive predictive value (95% CI, 75.10%-96.65%), 86.21% negative predictive value (95% CI, 75.07%-92.84%), and 87.64% overall accuracy, with substantial agreement (κ = 0.737, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

MRCP is highly specific for preoperative biliary mapping in LDLT donors but has limited sensitivity for variants, supporting routine IOC before ductal transection.

title: From Sudden Cardiac Death Prevention to Performance Optimization: A Conceptual Framework for Cardiovascular Assessment in Elite Athletes.
abstract: Cardiovascular pre-participation evaluation in elite athletes primarily aims to identify cardiovascular conditions associated with sudden cardiac death. Current international recommendations emphasize comprehensive medical history, physical examination, and resting 12-lead electrocardiography (ECG), with additional investigations guided by clini-cal findings and individual risk. However, advances in sports cardiology, cardiovascular imaging, and exercise physiology provide opportunities to integrate cardiovascular risk assessment with physiological performance evaluation. This article proposes a concep-tual, hypothesis-generating framework integrating structural, electrical, and functional cardiovascular assessment in elite athletes. The framework consists of 3 sequential components: comprehensive clinical assessment with resting ECG; transthoracic echo-cardiography for structural evaluation and longitudinal reference; and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) as an optional complementary investigation. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing may provide information on maximal oxygen uptake, ventilatory thresh-olds, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency, heart rate recovery, and exercise-induced arrhythmias, potentially supporting individualized training prescription and longitudinal physiological monitoring. Cardiac magnetic resonance and coronary computed tomog-raphy angiography (CCTA) may be considered selectively when clinically indicated. A one-time CCTA strategy during an athlete's career is proposed as a research hypothesis requiring prospective assessment of clinical utility and cost-effectiveness. Importantly, CPET and CCTA are not proposed as universal screening requirements. This framework is intended to complement, rather than replace, current evidence-based international recommendations. As the proposed model is based on available literature and expert opinion and has not undergone prospective clinical validation, future multicenter stud-ies are required to determine whether integrated cardiovascular assessment improves risk stratification, athlete safety, clinical decision-making, performance monitoring, and cost-effectiveness.

title: Growth hormone-releasing hormone-secreting giant pheochromocytoma causing acromegaly: a case report with a review of the literature.
abstract: The ectopic secretion of growth hormone (GH) or growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) is responsible for fewer than 1% of acromegaly cases. Furthermore, within this small population, GHRH-secreting pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas (PPGLs) are even rarer. A 57-year-old Japanese woman presented to our hospital for treatment of a large left-sided pheochromocytoma (PCC). A physical examination revealed enlargement of the nose and lips as well as macroglossia, thereby raising the suspicion of acromegaly, which was biochemically confirmed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a slightly enlarged pituitary gland but no definitive tumor. A left adrenalectomy was performed after careful dose titration of doxazosin and metyrosine. Postoperative biochemical improvement of GH excess and immunohistochemical analysis of the resected tumor confirmed the diagnosis of GHRH-secreting PCC. Given the possibility that PPGLs produce various ectopic hormones and peptides, thorough physical examinations remain fundamental for the accurate diagnosis and optimal management of patients with these tumors.

title: Multiple classification of childhood and juvenile autism spectrum disorder from ABIDE-II sMRI using BN-GO-CNN.
abstract: Objectives Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows heterogeneous neurodevelopmental patterns across childhood, juvenile development, and adulthood, so binary MRI classification may not fully capture age-and sex-related variation. This study proposes a proof-of-concept framework for multiple classification using ABIDE-II T1-weighted structural MRI (sMRI). Methods After image-quality screening, sMRI slices were processed using Canny edge detection, brain-region cropping, 224 × 224 resizing, and augmentation. Images were organized into sex-based four-class, age-based four-class, and combined age-and-sex eight-class datasets, separating child, young, juvenile, adult, male, and female groups. A Batch-Normalized Grid-Optimized CNN (BN-GO-CNN) was developed to learn structural representations directly from preprocessed sMRI, with grid search used to select key CNN hyperparameters. The model was compared with VGG16, DenseNet201, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 using identical image partitions. Results BN-GO-CNN achieved validation accuracies of 67.0 %, 64.0 %, and 60.5 % for sex-based, age-based, and combined age-and-sex classification, respectively. These outcomes remained above chance but showed limited class separability. Conclusions The modest performance suggests that label-related sMRI differences are subtle, supporting this framework as a preliminary test of CNN-assisted sMRI classification for future research use rather than a clinically reliable ASD diagnostic system.

title: Pulmonary CT classification based on CNN and Grad-CAM explainability using VGG16 and MobileNetV2.
abstract: Objectives This study compared the classification performance of VGG16 and MobileNetV2 models for normal-versus-lung-cancer-positive pulmonary CT image classification, with Grad-CAM used for post-hoc visual explainability. Methods A hospital-provided dataset of 550 non-contrast thoracic CT images, comprising 240 normal and 310 lung cancer-positive images, was divided into training, validation and test subsets using a patient-grouped stratified 50/10/40 split. Images were acquired at 120 kV with a 512 × 512 matrix using a NeuViz 128 CT scanner. Both models used the same preprocessing, training-only augmentation and evaluation protocol. The VGG16 model used stacked convolutional blocks, whereas MobileNetV2 used inverted residual bottlenecks with global average pooling, dropout and a sigmoid classification layer. Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, balanced accuracy, ROC-AUC, MCC and Cohen's kappa, while Grad-CAM examined decision-relevant regions. Results On the 220-image independent test set, VGG16 achieved 0.9636 accuracy, 0.9677 sensitivity, 0.9583 specificity and 0.9569 ROC-AUC. MobileNetV2 achieved 0.9909 accuracy, 0.9919 sensitivity, 0.9896 specificity and 0.9858 ROC-AUC, with fewer false-positive and false-negative predictions. Conclusions MobileNetV2 achieved stronger held-out test performance than VGG16 under identical experimental conditions. Larger multi-centre patient-level validation remains necessary before clinical deployment in CT screening workflows.

title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
abstract: Introduction RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Content This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning. Summary Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs. Outlook Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

title: Pediatric prolactinoma-associated pituitary apoplexy presenting with acute visual loss: a case report, literature review, and management strategy.
abstract: Objectives Hemorrhagic pituitary apoplexy (PA) in children is exceedingly rare, with approximately 32 cases reported since 1980. Current guidelines recommend cabergoline as first-line therapy; however, acute complete visual loss mandates emergency surgical decompression. No guideline defines the optimal extent of resection, despite gross total resection carrying a 48-54 % risk of panhypopituitarism. Case presentation An 11-year-old prepubertal girl presented with a 2-day history of complete right-eye visual loss. Serum prolactin was 987 μg/L, and MRI demonstrated a hemorrhagic sellar-suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm. Emergency endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery was performed with an intentionally limited strategy - hematoma evacuation, optic decompression, and partial debulking - deliberately avoiding aggressive capsular dissection. Histopathology confirmed prolactinoma. Vision was fully restored immediately after extubation, with near-complete visual field recovery on postoperative day 5 (VFI 98 %). Adrenocortical function was preserved. Central hypothyroidism developed, and levothyroxine was initiated. Cabergoline (0.25 mg/week) was started on postoperative day 5, achieving a 93.7 % prolactin reduction by day 20 (987 → 61.9 μg/L). Conclusions In pediatric prolactinoma-associated PA requiring emergency surgery, a decompression-first strategy prioritizing visual rescue and tissue diagnosis over gross total resection may reduce the risk of panhypopituitarism, with residual tumor subsequently managed with cabergoline. The rapid biochemical response documented here supports this approach, though multicenter prospective evaluation is required.

title: FSH-secreting pituitary adenomas presenting with spontaneous ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in children and adolescents: two cases, a literature review, and long-term follow-up.
abstract: Functioning FSH-secreting pituitary adenomas (FSHomas) are exceedingly rare in children; only nine pediatric patients, seven girls and two boys, have been reported previously. In girls, they commonly present with spontaneous ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (sOHSS). The clinical presentation, management, and long-term outcomes of these tumors remain incompletely characterized. We report two girls aged 10.1 and 16 years with prolonged menstrual bleeding and bilateral multicystic ovarian enlargement due to FSHoma-associated sOHSS. Both demonstrated markedly elevated estradiol, suppressed LH, and nonsuppressed (inappropriately normal) FSH, with pituitary adenomas of 14 × 11 × 13 mm and 9 × 9 mm on MRI; immunohistochemistry was FSHβ-positive in both. Case 1 underwent transsphenoidal adenectomy after medical treatment with letrozole and cabergoline; despite residual tumor tissue, she remained stable over 10 years of follow-up. Case 2 underwent transsphenoidal resection but developed recurrent hyperestrogenism and ovarian enlargement 5 years later despite radiological stability of the residual adenoma, and subsequently required emergency surgery for ovarian torsion (excision of the left ovary, right ovarian cystectomy). All 11 pediatric patients, including the present two, were compared for presentation, treatment, and long-term outcome. These cases provide 10 and 9 years of follow-up after diagnosis. Biochemical recurrence may occur independently of radiological tumor progression, and persistent ovarian stimulation from residual adenoma tissue may cause irreversible complications, including ovarian torsion. Long-term multidisciplinary surveillance with serial hormonal assessment, pelvic imaging, and pituitary MRI is essential, and early pituitary-directed intervention may prevent unnecessary gynecological surgery.

title: Magnetoencephalography in Parkinson's disease: diagnostic potential and barriers to clinical translation.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder with motor and nonmotor manifestations. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, and validated markers of early disease and subsequent progression are still needed. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures neuronal magnetic fields with millisecond temporal resolution and provides a means of characterizing cortical dysfunction. This narrative review critically synthesizes MEG evidence on periodic and aperiodic spectral activity, functional connectivity, network topology, and individual brain fingerprinting, with emphasis on diagnostic relevance and barriers to clinical translation. Recurring findings include spectral slowing and cognitive-network disruption, whereas resting β power, burst dynamics, and coupling depend on clinical phenotype, treatment state, and analytical choices. Evidence from electroencephalogram (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and invasive recordings is distinguished from direct MEG findings. Internally validated classification of established PD and healthy controls is promising, but does not establish performance in prodromal disease or clinically uncertain parkinsonism. Optically pumped magnetometers may improve recording flexibility while retaining requirements for environmental interference control. Prospective clinical cohorts, standardized acquisition and analysis, reproducibility studies, independent validation, and comparison with clinical assessment are needed to establish incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility.

title: Lung ultrasound B-lines and serum KL-6 in the management of connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease.
abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with connective tissue diseases (CTDs). Early diagnosis, appropriate intervention, and close monitoring are critical to mitigate the progression of CTD-ILD. Lung ultrasound (LUS) B-lines and serum Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6) have emerged as promising, non-invasive, and radiation-free biomarkers for ILD. This single-center retrospective study aimed to evaluate the combined diagnostic and assessment value of B-lines and KL-6 in patients with CTD-ILD. A total of 226 consecutive patients with CTD who underwent high resolution computed tomography (HRCT), LUS and serum KL-6 testing within a one-month interval were retrospectively enrolled. Based on HRCT findings, patients were classified into ILD and non-ILD groups. Those with ILD were further subdivided into fibrotic ILD (F-ILD) and non-fibrotic ILD (NF-ILD) according to radiographic patterns. LUS was performed across 50 scanning sites, and the total number of B-lines was calculated as a B-lines number. Correlations between B-lines number, KL-6 level, and HRCT Warrick score were analyzed. The diagnostic accuracy of LUS B-lines and KL-6, individually and in combination, for detecting ILD and F-ILD was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The ability of B-lines and KL-6 to discriminate ILD severity based on the HRCT Warrick score was assessed. The ILD group demonstrated significantly higher B-lines number and serum KL-6 levels compared to the non-ILD group (P < 0.001). ROC analysis showed good diagnostic performance for both B-lines (AUC = 0.85 [95% CI: 0.80-0.90]; sensitivity = 77.6%; specificity = 77.0%) and KL-6 (AUC = 0.79 [95% CI: 0.73-0.85]; sensitivity = 58.6%; specificity = 91.9%). The combination of both markers further improved diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.87 [95% CI: 0.82-0.91]; sensitivity = 74.3%; specificity = 86.5%). Both B-lines number and KL-6 level showed significant positive correlations with the HRCT Warrick score. Notably, B-lines number and serum KL-6 were able to distinguish between F-ILD and NF-ILD subtypes (both P < 0.001) and were associated with disease severity (P < 0.001 for B-lines; P = 0.016 for KL-6). Both LUS B-lines and serum KL-6 are valuable biomarkers for diagnosing and assessing CTD-ILD, and their combination enhances diagnostic accuracy.

title: Regional Brain Structural Changes During the Transition from Acute to Chronic Neuropathic Pain: A Longitudinal Study in a Rat Model of Orofacial Pain.
abstract: Brain imaging studies have identified structural alterations in individuals with chronic neuropathic pain, particularly in regions involved in sensory, emotional, and cognitive processing. However, most studies remain cross-sectional, leaving the temporal progression of these changes during pain chronification unclear. This gap is critical, as both neural and non-neural cells undergo dynamic changes during pain chronification. The primary aim of this study was to track longitudinally regional brain volume and density changes before and after induction of orofacial neuropathic pain in male rats, using a chronic constriction injury of the infraorbital nerve (ION-CCI). This model enables assessment of changes in the spinal trigeminal nucleus (SpVn). T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans were acquired 7 d prior to injury and then at +2, +7, +14, and +28 d, in ION-CCI ( n = 11), sham-injured ( n = 6), and naive ( n = 8) groups. Voxel-based and deformation-based morphometry were used to identify early- and late-onset density and volumetric changes, respectively. Early after injury, transient, bidirectional volume and/or density changes in the ipsilateral primary somatosensory cortex (S1), contralateral SpVn, and bilateral dorsomedial periaqueductal gray, ipsilateral retrosplenial and contralateral prelimbic cortices, were observed. In contrast, late-onset changes were more widespread, with volume increases observed bilaterally in the SpVn pars interpolaris (SpVo), in the ipsilateral dorsomedial SpVn (SpVdm), bilateral lateral hypothalamus, and contralateral amygdalo-hippocampal complex, and volume decreases in contralateral retrosplenial, prelimbic, and bilateral S1 cortices. These findings reveal early dynamic reorganization of sensory and sensory-modulatory brain regions, followed by sustained structural alterations across trigeminal brainstem nuclei, limbic-hypothalamic systems, and higher-order cortical networks.

title: Intracranial germ cell tumours presenting with AVP deficiency and evolving panhypopituitarism: diagnostic pitfalls in early imaging and biopsy.
abstract: We report three Chinese children with central nervous system germ cell tumours (CNS GCTs) presenting as arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency with or without pituitary stalk thickening, initially diagnosed as lymphocytic hypophysitis (LyH) and idiopathic AVP deficiency. Case 1 showed conflicting biopsy results, suggesting hypophysitis and then germinoma. Case 2 had one negative transsphenoidal biopsy and later one biopsy finding LyH before suprasellar mass diagnosis. Case 3 had a normal initial MRI brain and was followed up as idiopathic AVP deficiency but found to have extensive tumour the next year. All patients achieved remission with chemotherapy and radiotherapy but sustained lifelong panhypopituitarism. Asia has a higher prevalence of CNS GCTs in children. Pituitary stalk thickening with risk factors including pituitary stalk thickness ≥6.5 mm, AVP deficiency, two or more pituitary hormone deficiencies at presentation, and evolving hypopituitarism mandates a high level of malignant suspicion even if prior histopathology is negative. In ethnic groups where the prevalence of CNS GCT is higher, biopsy should be offered when presented with risk factors. These cases highlight pitfalls of false-negative MRI and biopsy, emphasising epidemiology-informed diagnostic algorithms to prevent diagnostic delays.

title: A review of digital orthopedic techniques in pre- and intra-operative management of scaphoid fracture.
abstract: Digital orthopedics integrates artificial intelligence, finite element analysis, virtual surgical planning, intraoperative navigation, robotics, and three-dimensional printing into a precise, individualized workflow for scaphoid fracture management. Artificial intelligence-based algorithms achieve high diagnostic accuracy for scaphoid fractures on plain radiographs, aid in detecting occult fractures, and support treatment decisions. Three-dimensional fracture mapping and finite element analysis enable quantitative assessment of fracture morphology and biomechanical stability, supporting individualized preoperative planning. Computer-assisted navigation reduces radiation exposure and guidewire attempts compared with conventional fluoroscopy but remains limited by registration inaccuracy and dependence on manual execution. Robot-assisted surgery improves procedural consistency and screw accuracy, with a learning curve of approximately 10-20 cases; however, it is constrained by longer setup times, high costs, and predominantly level IV evidence. Virtual surgical planning combined with three-dimensional printing provides patient-specific percutaneous guides, reduction templates, anatomical models, and custom prostheses, improving accuracy, reducing radiation exposure, and enabling motion-preserving salvage for scaphoid nonunions and scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse. Current evidence is largely based on small case series and cadaveric studies, highlighting the need for standardized protocols and high-quality comparative trials to support widespread adoption.

title: Management of Nondiagnostic Thyroid Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology Nodules Based on TI-RADS Risk Assessment.
abstract: Objective The high prevalence of thyroid nodules and the frequent occurrence of nondiagnostic (ND) results on fine-needle aspiration (FNA) necessitates malignancy risk stratification to balance cancer detection while avoiding unnecessary repeat biopsies. This study evaluated malignancy rates and management strategies for nodules with ND cytology, stratified by the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS) score. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 342 consecutive patients with initial ND ultrasound-guided (USG) thyroid FNA from a high volume, two-practitioner clinic between January 2019 and June 2024. Data collected from chart review included Bethesda cytopathology classifications, management approaches, and final histopathological diagnosis when available. Results Among 3717 thyroid FNAs performed during the study period, 342 (9.2%) were ND on initial sampling. TI-RADS (TR) distribution for ND nodules was: TR1 9.6%, TR2 9.9%, TR3 28.1%, TR4 45.3%, TR5 7.0%. Initial management comprised repeat FNA in 170 (49.7%) patients, ultrasound (US) surveillance in 101 (29.5%), surgery in 17 (5.0%); 54 (15.8%) patients were lost to follow-up. Of repeat FNAs, 47 (27.6%) remained ND. Among 33 surgical cases, malignancy was identified in 6 (1.8%) index nodules with initial ND cytology. Five malignancies occurred in TR4 nodules and one in a TR5 nodule. Importantly, there were no malignancies among 17 resected TR1-3 nodules. Conclusion For experienced practitioners in a high-volume clinic, ND thyroid FNA cytology carries a low overall observed risk of malignancy (1.8%). TI-RADS scores should be taken into consideration to guide management decisions for ND cytology nodules between repeat FNA, US surveillance, or surgery.
