title: Habitat Radiomics-Based Stacking Ensemble Model for Predicting Disease-Free Survival in Early-Stage Cervical Cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose Despite undergoing curative surgery, about 30% of patients with early-stage cervical cancer (ECC) face the risk of recurrence. However, current prognostic tools are not very effective, with concordance index (C-index) typically ranging from 0.60 to 0.70. This study aimed to develop and validate a stacking survival ensemble model that incorporates intratumoral and peritumoral habitat radiomic features derived from routine preoperative multiparametric MRI to predict postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) in ECC. Methods This retrospective-prospective study enrolled 583 ECC patients (training: n = 293, internal validation: n = 165, external validation: n = 125). Habitat radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and 3-mm peritumoral regions on preoperative T2WI, DWI, and CE-T1WI. A two-tier stacking survival ensemble framework was constructed with five base survival models (Cox regression, Random Survival Forest, Elastic Net-Cox, DeepSurv, and Support Vector Regression) and a Cox regression Meta-learner. Performance was assessed by C-index, time-dependent AUC, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. The incremental value of the model-derived lymph node metastasis probability (pLNM) from our prior classification model was also evaluated. Results The Meta-model achieved C-indices of 0.878, 0.868, and 0.848 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, outperforming most base models (P < 0.05). Externally, it yielded time-dependent AUCs of 0.887, 0.875, and 0.860 at 12, 24, and 36 months. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the Meta-model effectively stratified into high- and low-risk groups with distinct DFS outcomes (log-rank P < 0.001 for all cohorts). Adding pLNM further improved C-index from 0.878 to 0.913 in the training cohort (P < 0.001). Conclusion The stacking survival ensemble model enables accurate postoperative risk stratification for ECC patients using routine preoperative MRI without additional imaging, potentially guiding individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance intensity.

title: SAM-NeuroAdapt: an atlas-guided, training-free pipeline for skull-stripping in infant and adult MRI
abstract: Abstract Skull-stripping, the removal of non-brain tissue from magnetic resonance images, is an early step of most neuroimaging pipelines whose errors propagate to later measurements. However, current methods such as HD-BET, SynthStrip and LifespanStrip depend on task-specific training on large image collections. To test how much of this benefit survives without training, this study presents SAM-NeuroAdapt, a training-free pipeline. First, an age-matched template is selected from a library of 21 atlases and registered to the image. The registered atlas then supplies the prompts of a frozen Segment Anything Model 2, and the mask is refined by classical boundary correction. The pipeline was compared with HD-BET on three whole-head benchmarks, with multiplicity-adjusted p-values. On infants (Baby Open Brains, 71 visits, 51 participants), it achieved higher Dice (0.920 versus 0.905) and a lower average symmetric surface distance (ASSD; 2.07 versus 5.11 mm). On adults, no Dice difference was detected; ASSD was ower on Mindboggle-101 (n = 101) and, under one of two adjustment procedures, on IBSR-20 (n = 20). Furthermore, an ablation showed that the age-matched atlas alone reached the infant Dice of the complete pipeline (0.923 versus 0.920), while the remaining stages reduced infant surface distances by 36–46%; without atlas guidance, 26–100% of cases failed. These findings indicate that atlas matching, rather than the foundation model, drives overlap accuracy and that a well-matched atlas is a competitive training-free baseline. Two eval-uation pitfalls are also documented: a surface-distance definition that rewards over-segmentation and benchmarks distributed already skull-stripped

title: Assessment of the Clinical Role of Serum Levels of IL-1, VEGF, and MMP-2 in the Detection of Radiation Pneumonitis and Prediction of Its Occurrence in Breast Cancer Females Treated with Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background Radiation pneumonitis (RP) represents a significant complication of breast cancer radiotherapy. Interleukin-1 (IL-1), matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2), and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) are key mediators of radiation-induced lung injury. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and predictive utility of serum IL-1, VEGF, and MMP-2 levels for RP in breast cancer patients undergoing postoperative radiotherapy. Methods This prospective case-control study enrolled 55 females (20 healthy controls, 35 breast cancer patients). Serum biomarkers were measured using ELISA before radiotherapy (RT), immediately after RT, and at six-month follow-up. Patients were monitored for RP development using clinical assessment and computed tomography. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined diagnostic performance and optimal cut-off values. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors of RP. Results Serum IL-1, VEGF, and MMP-2 showed non-significant elevations in breast cancer patients before RT compared with controls. All three biomarkers increased significantly after RT (P < 0.05). At six months post-RT, patients who developed RP (n = 9, 25.7%) had significantly higher serum IL-1 (118.61 ± 15.79 vs. 53.08 ± 3.63 ng/ml, P < 0.001) and MMP-2 (2491.22 ± 203.15 vs. 1331.83 ± 99.66 ng/ml, P < 0.001) compared with those without RP, while VEGF showed no significant difference. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent predictive performance for IL-1 (AUC = 0.958, cut-off = 69.44 ng/ml, sensitivity = 90%, specificity = 84%) and MMP-2 (AUC = 0.932, cut-off = 1204.67 ng/ml, sensitivity = 88.9%, specificity = 69.6%). Multivariate analysis identified pre-RT IL-1 > 69.44 ng/ml (OR = 8.42, 95% CI: 2.14–33.18, P = 0.002) and MMP-2 > 1204.67 ng/ml (OR = 6.75, 95% CI: 1.89–24.12, P = 0.003) as independent predictors of RP. A combined biomarker model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.981, P < 0.001). Conclusions Pre-radiotherapy serum IL-1 and MMP-2 levels are robust independent predictors of radiation pneumonitis in breast cancer patients. A combined biomarker approach enhances predictive accuracy and may facilitate personalized risk stratification and early intervention strategies.

title: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Presenting with Spontaneous Pneumothorax and Osteolytic Lesions: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare myeloid neoplasm characterized by a highly heterogeneous clinical presentation, ranging from localized osseous lesions to multisystem disease involving high-risk organs. We report the case of a two-year-old girl who presented with persistent fever, dyspnea, and irritability. Initial chest radiography demonstrated a diffuse bilateral reticulonodular pulmonary pattern. During hospitalization, she developed a spontaneous right-sided pneumothorax associated with complete right lung atelectasis. Chest computed tomography revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary cystic lesions, while radiographs of the skull and long bones demonstrated multiple well-defined osteolytic lesions without periosteal reaction. The diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis was confirmed by histopathological examination. Despite intensive supportive management, the patient died seven days after admission because of severe pulmonary involvement. This case highlights the pivotal role of diagnostic imaging in the early recognition of multisystem LCH and underscores the importance of considering this entity in pediatric patients presenting with cystic lung disease accompanied by lytic bone lesions, as prompt diagnosis may facilitate appropriate management and improve clinical outcomes.

title: MCP-MedImg: Enabling Standardized PACS-AI Integration through the Model Context Protocol
abstract: Abstract Background: The proliferation of AI-assisted diagnostic models in medical imaging has created a fragmented integration landscape with PACS systems, leading to redundant development, inconsistent security compliance, and disconnected clinical workflows. Most AI diagnostic products exist as standalone Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), limiting scalability, auditability, and clinical adoption. Existing integration solutions (Direct Plugin, DICOM Router, VNA) are point-to-point adaptations without unified semantic layers. While the Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides tool invocation frameworks for AI agents, it lacks dedicated extensions for the medical imaging domain. Critically, global regulators (FDA, NMPA, EU) are converging on total product life cycle (TPLC) approaches demanding continuous post-market surveillance, yet no standardized protocol supports such surveillance at scale. Objective: We propose MCP-MedImg, an open reference architecture and protocol specification for interoperable integration and governance of AI services in medical imaging ecosystems, allowing AI capabilities to be discovered, invoked, monitored, and governed across heterogeneous healthcare environments without replacing existing PACS infrastructures. Methods: MCP-MedImg extends MCP with a four-layer architecture: Transport (DICOMweb-compatible, with dicom-mcp upward compatibility), Security and Compliance (PHI de-identification plus 14-column audit trail), AI Orchestration (model routing and version management), and Application Semantics (inspection-driven routing, lesion encoding, conditional human-in-the-loop verification). The specification defines six core information model entities and a tiered conformance model (five mandatory requirements, seven optional extensions). A reference implementation based on Orthanc PACS and nnU-Net validates protocol consistency, workflow, multi-model routing, DICOM SR/SEG generation, and audit trails. Results: The reference implementation demonstrated end-to-end interoperability, standardized service registration, structured result integration (DICOM SR/SEG), and auditable tracking of AI lifecycle events. On an NVIDIA RTX 4090 D, end-to-end latency under realistic clinical conditions was: LIDC-IDRI lung nodule CT (200 volumes, mean 5.4 s, P99 22.6 s) and MSD Heart cardiac MRI (10 volumes, mean 18.2 s, P99 27.6 s, 5-fold ensemble Dice 0.9324). Validation comprised 132 passing tests across 10 verification scenarios. Conclusions: MCP-MedImg aims to transform AI-assisted diagnosis from standalone software into auditable, service-oriented capabilities with conditional human-in-the-loop verification—directly addressing the regulatory surveillance gap and establishing foundations for governable public infrastructure in healthcare AI. By defining a tiered conformance model, the protocol enables incremental adoption: from minimal compliance (Level 1) through full production deployment (Level 3). The service-oriented delivery model, with built-in audit trails, configurable verification, and standardized output generation, significantly enhances clinical trust, lowers deployment barriers, and accelerates the adoption of AI-assisted diagnosis in routine clinical practice.

title: Evaluation Metrics for Image Classification, Segmentation and Localization Mathematical Foundations, Comparative Analysis and Research Recommendations
abstract: Abstract Evaluation metrics dictate the incentives for an image analysis system, detect remaining failures, and verify any proposed improvement in scientific or clinical claims. Despite the mathematical similarity of classification, segmentation, and localization, the units, matching criteria, and practice implications vary across these tasks. The current review analyzes the distinctions through the lens of a selected sample of 150 bibliographically validated references, including 10 papers from the provided author profile. It incorporates foundational statistics, state-of-the-art benchmarking practices, medical imaging use cases, and recent developments in uncertainties, selective prediction, and deployment. The review organizes 72 metrics and corresponding evaluation quantities by the question they answer: correctness of decision, score discrimination, reliability of probabilities, spatial correspondence, recovery of objects, localization of geometry, or practical utility. Comparisons describe equations, assumptions, aggregation approaches, advantages, and failures. Ten deterministic worked examples demonstrate prevalence effects, constant discrimination and worsening probability scores, reverse rankings because of aggregation, hidden border failures by overlap, detection matching, physical landmark errors, and the cost of abstaining. Twenty-four numeric instances from 4 separate publications supply additional citations and examples without pooling the inconsistent results. The primary takeaway is that a sound evaluation requires a small and preselected set of metrics, complementary to each other, applicable to the defined population, unit, reference standard, and decision. For classification, operating point performance is always required, along with discrimination and probability metrics. Segmentation demands appropriate measures of overlap, borders, and object topology. Localization needs explicitly stated criteria of correspondence and tolerance and false positive control. Independent partitioning, uncertainties, subgroups, and workflow outputs determine the interpretability of the metrics. This manuscript is an organized critical review and methodology resource, but not a completed systematic review according to PRISMA criteria, meta-analysis, or benchmark of a new model. The attached list of metrics, reference export, extraction notes, computational code, and reporting checklist help design and validate reproducible studies and author reviews.

Despite the mathematical similarity of classification, segmentation, and localization, the units, matching criteria, and practice implications vary across these tasks. title: Bounded Repair Reachability of Residual Critical Blocks in 3D Binary Masks under SAFE-Gated Single-Voxel Flips
abstract: Abstract Critical configurations in three-dimensional binary images violate digital well-composedness, and voxel repairs can conflict with path constraints and foreground preservation. We formulate bounded repair reachability under single-voxel flips preserving the homotopy type of the foreground complex. We establish relations among admissible path sets and show that, under flip-once, endpoint and pathwise fidelity yield identical successful instances and shortest successful depths. Breadth-first search distinguishes found repairs, bounded absence and resource-limited outcomes. On 680 residual blocks from 222 Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2021 masks, unrestricted searches within radius 2 and depth 6 find repairs for 72 blocks under endpoint fidelity and 15 under pathwise fidelity. An endpoint-faithful witness temporarily removes and restores input foreground; a completed search excludes pathwise-faithful repair of that block within these bounds. These results distinguish the topological validity of moves from the admissibility of repair paths. Conclusions are limited to the stated windows, horizons and moves.

title: Deep Learning-Based Breast Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation Using Cross-Scale Attention and Edge-Aware Supervision
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate segmentation of breast lesions in ultrasound is complicated by variations in lesion morphology, speckle noise, and indistinct margins. Objective To describe and assess a modified Attention U-Net combining spatial token mixing, squeeze-and-excitation attention, Polar/Log-Polar geometric features, large-kernel context aggregation, cross-scale attention, and auxiliary edge prediction. Materials and Methods The architecture was evaluated using the publicly available Breast Ultrasound Images Dataset (BUSI). The submitted manuscript does not specify the number of unique patients, patient-level data partitioning, or independent external validation; these details must be confirmed before submission. Results Reported test-set pixel accuracy was 0.9808 and specificity 0.9935, but Dice overlap was 0.3673, intersection-over-union (IoU) was 0.2250, precision was 0.4674, and recall was 0.3026. Table 1 reports ROC-AUC 0.9005, whereas the ROC figure reports 0.9479; this discrepancy requires verification against saved test predictions. Conclusion Although the architecture combines multiple context- and edge-sensitive mechanisms, the observed tumor overlap and sensitivity are insufficient to demonstrate reliable clinical lesion delineation. Controlled segmentation-baseline experiments, ablations, and independent validation are required before clinical claims can be made.

title: Central nervous system aspergillosis with negative serum fungal biomarkers after sequential teclistamab and talquetamab for multiple myeloma: a case report and review of the literature
abstract: Abstract Bispecific antibodies directed against B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D) have improved outcomes in relapsed multiple myeloma but are associated with a high burden of infection. Invasive mould infection of the central nervous system (CNS) has rarely been described in this setting. We report a 70-year-old woman with heavily pretreated IgG-kappa myeloma who received teclistamab, complicated by immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) treated with corticosteroids, followed by talquetamab. She received antiviral and anti- Pneumocystis prophylaxis and intravenous immunoglobulin, without mould-active cover. Shortly after starting talquetamab, she developed cough and confusion, with cavitating pulmonary lesions initially attributed to bacterial abscesses. Serum galactomannan remained 0.1 on serial testing and β-D-glucan was negative. Computed tomography-guided lung biopsy confirmed pulmonary aspergillosis, and voriconazole was started. Failure to regain her functional baseline and progressive weakness, initially difficult to separate from her previous ICANS, led to brain magnetic resonance imaging, which showed a 10-mm ring-enhancing occipital lesion. Biopsy confirmed CNS aspergillosis. A literature review identified few published cases of invasive aspergillosis during bispecific therapy for myeloma, and serum galactomannan was positive in those with reported results. Negative fungal biomarkers should not exclude invasive aspergillosis in patients receiving bispecific antibodies, and new neurological decline warrants imaging and tissue diagnosis even after ICANS. Patients who require corticosteroids for ICANS during bispecific therapy, particularly after sequential bispecific exposure, may warrant individualised assessment of invasive mould risk and consideration of azole prophylaxis, pending prospective evaluation.

title: Functional and MRI improvement followed by a mixed trajectory during cannabinoid-terpenoid exposure in glioblastoma: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Glioblastoma has limited salvage options, while viable tumour, treatment injury, postoperative change, oedema and corticosteroid effects may produce overlapping clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings. Materials and Methods: Clinical records, serial MRI examinations and signed radiology reports were reviewed descriptively for a patient with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-promoter-methylated glioblastoma. The exposure history and contemporaneously documented neurological findings were aligned with seven MRI time points. No blinded central review, standardised volumetry or formal RANO 2.0 adjudication was performed. Results: After two operations, radiotherapy, concomitant temozolomide and three adjuvant cycles, serial MRI documented progression before April 2025. During a non-standard exposure state comprising intranasal perillyl alcohol and alpha-bisabolol, individualised cannabinoids and docosahexaenoic acid/medium-chain triglyceride oil, with dexamethasone fixed at 2 mg/day, hemiplegia/KPS 50 improved to hemiparesis with regained walking/KPS 80, coinciding with reduced enhancement. Later MRI showed increasing right temporal and cerebellar enhancement, including a new contralateral cerebellar focus, despite substantially stable postoperative cavity and T2/FLAIR extent. June 2026 lesion perfusion curves were low-amplitude without pathological hyperperfusion. The patient subsequently died after an overall survival of 45 months. Conclusions: This uncontrolled case documents early functional and radiological improvement on a stable corticosteroid background, followed by an anatomically progressive but biologically indeterminate trajectory. It does not establish treatment causality, survival benefit, formal tumour response or component-specific efficacy; mixed viable tumour and treatment effect or radiation necrosis could not be excluded. Although this single case does not establish a verified benefit the observed overall survival reached a time span of extraordinarily 45 months.

title: Neural correlates of empathy in autism: a coordinate-based meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose . Autistic and non-autistic people often differ in how readily they understand one another’s intentions and emotional states. Although empathy is commonly invoked to explain these differences, which components of empathic processing differ in autism, and their neural underpinnings, remain unclear. Methods . We conducted a pre-registered coordinate-based meta-analysis (activation likelihood estimation; ALE) of task-based fMRI studies of empathy in autism, examining within-group convergence, conjunction and between-group divergence separately for affective and cognitive components. Eleven studies (12 independent samples) met inclusion criteria, comprising 213 autistic and 216 non-autistic participants and 600 foci across 35 experiments; a multi-agent AI second reviewer supported screening and extraction. Results . Both groups shared a core empathy network (precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex, right middle temporal gyrus/posterior superior temporal sulcus, left inferior frontal gyrus, dorsomedial paracingulate), but the rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a canonical cognitive-empathy hub, converged only in non-autistic participants. The between-group contrast was strongly asymmetric: non-autistic participants exceeded autistic convergence in ten regions, eight of them cognitive-empathy nodes, the largest in rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; autistic participants exceeded non-autistic convergence in one region only, the posterior right temporoparietal junction. Subdomain analyses indicated relatively preserved convergence for affective empathy, with sparser, more diffuse overlap for cognitive empathy. Conclusion . These findings are consistent with a dissociation between relatively preserved affective and altered cognitive empathy in autism, and suggest a redistribution of activation within the mentalizing network rather than a global absence of empathy-related processing. Key words: autism spectrum disorder; empathy; activation likelihood estimation; functional magnetic resonance imaging; dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; temporoparietal junction

title: Robot-Pet and Virtual Reality Distraction During Fissure Sealant Treatment in Children: A Three-Arm Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: Abstract Innovative distraction approaches are increasingly being explored in pediatric dentistry. This three-arm randomized controlled trial aimed to compare Robot-Pet and virtual reality (VR) distraction with Tell-Show-Do (TSD) during children's first dental treatment involving fissure sealant placement. Of the 78 randomized children aged 6-10 years, 72 completed treatment and were analyzed (24/group). Dental anxiety(DA) levels were assessed using the Children's Fear Survey Schedule-Dental Subscale (CFSS-DS) and Facial Image Scale (FIS), and behavior using the Frankl Behavior Rating Scale (FBRS), pre- and post-treatment. Intraoperative behavior was evaluated using the Modified Houpt Scale (MHS) during treatment, while heart rate and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) were measured before, during, and after treatment. Post-treatment perceptions were assessed by questionnaire. Analyses used Chi-square/Fisher’s exact, Kruskal-Wallis, and Brunner-Langer models with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (p<0.05). CFSS-DS and FIS scores decreased post-treatment in all groups (p<0.05), with no between-group differences (p>0.05). VR had lower MHS-Movement scores than Robot-Pet and Control (p<0.05). Heart rate and oxygen saturation did not differ between groups (p>0.05); heart rate increased during washing compared with pre-treatment across groups (p<0.05). Children and parents positively evaluated Robot-Pet and VR. DA scores decreased post-treatment in all groups without between-group differences. Robot-Pet offers tactile distraction, whereas VR provides audiovisual distraction and was associated with less movement during treatment. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT06243705), registered on 25 January 2024 (retrospectively registered).

title: Exploring the Spectrum of Clinical and Radiological Findings in Active Tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract Background Clinical data may not accurately diagnose pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), mainly due to manifestation overlap with other diseases, causing delays and misdiagnoses. Many gaps in the interpretation of clinical and radiographic findings were addressed and updated in our study. Methods An institutional-based study was carried out between 02/01/2018 and 26/06/2020 to clinically assess TB outpatients in high-burden zones. Those patients were identified through smear microscopy, GeneXpert Ultra, and chest X-rays and TB positives were interviewed. Of total, 329 patients were enrolled from Bench-Skeko, 23 from Skeka, and 29 from Keffa. Both descriptive and inferential statistics were performed using Stata 14/16. Results A total of 410 TB confirmed cases, with 328 (80%) being PTB, 79 (19.3%) EPTB, and 3 (0.73%) involving both forms were involved in this study. The mean age was 27.65 ± 11.44 years, with 55% male. Most patients were recently identified (99.3%). GeneXpert was used in 62.4%, AFB in 8.78%, and lesion biopsy or FNAC for EPTB in 16.83%, and 98% was on the intensive therapy for susceptible TB. A febrile episode was diagnosed in 93% (5.4% >40°C, 87% <39°C), night sweat in 93.17%, appetite loss in 89%, fatigue in 90%, and weight loss in 88%. Respiratory symptoms were very common, with cough reported in 94.2%: productive in 91%, and prolonged (> 3 wks) in 77%. Abnormalities in chest X ray were reported in 16.3%, with pleural effusion in 11.2%, cavitary formations in 13%, and lymph node enlarged in 14%. Blood pressure abnormalities were relatively low, with 76.3% having normal. Only few findings were reported as statistically significant predictors of active PTB. Chest abnormalities (OR = 6.87), prolonged cough (OR = 6.4), mucoid (OR = 14.6), and mucopurulent sputum (OR = 56.4) increased PTB odds, while lymphadenopathy was less commonly reported (OR = 0.16). Appetite loss (OR = 3.26), pleural effusion (OR = 2.41), and fibrosis (OR = 2.31) showed weak associations. Conclusions A high prevalence of the TB tetrad: prolonged cough, night sweat, fever and appetite loss were observed. PTB odds were higher with chest abnormalities, effusion, fibrosis, infiltration, and expansion, highlighting the diagnostic value of radiology. Clinical Trial Registration : No applicable

title: Unsupervised multimodal brain MRI registration with complementary learned and structural descriptors.
abstract: Abstract Deformable registration of T1- and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance images is difficult because tissue intensities differ across contrasts. We investigate whether learned and hand-crafted descriptors provide complementary similarity information for unsupervised registration. A Cross-Modal Descriptor Network learns contrast-invariant voxel embeddings through self-supervised contrastive training on aligned same-subject pairs. These embeddings are combined with the modality-independent neighbourhood descriptor with self-similarity context (MIND-SSC) to train a compact diffeomorphic attention U-Net without anatomical labels. In inter-subject T1-to-T2 registration on the IXI dataset (n=45), the hybrid achieved a mean Dice coefficient of 0.700 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance of 3.21 mm, with no observed folded voxels. It outperformed the evaluated classical, learned, structural-descriptor, transformer, and foundation-model baselines (p<0.05, paired Wilcoxon tests). Gains were largest for small deep gray-matter structures, and the hybrid also performed best in the evaluated unseen-scanner and BraTS glioma experiments. Descriptors are used only during training; inference requires one 83 ms forward pass of a 0.247 M-parameter network. These results support combining learned and structural descriptors for accurate and computationally efficient multimodal brain registration.

title: Conditions for Pharmacological Sanctuaries in Perivascular Tumour Cords: A Reaction–Diffusion Analysis, a Regrowth-Kinetics Identity, and a Descriptive Survival Analysis of Histologic Subtype in Resected Lung Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background: Adjuvant osimertinib markedly improves disease-free survival in resected EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, extended follow-up in the ADAURA trial revealed that among patients who experienced disease recurrence, the majority of relapses manifested after planned treatment cessation at year 3, frequently without acquired secondary genomic resistance mutations. We examined whether biophysical drug transport limitations could establish tissue sanctuaries that shelter drug-sensitive tumor cells. Methods: We analyzed steady-state reaction–diffusion transport in two canonical tumor micro-architectures: out-ward perivascular cords (divergent cylindrical geometry, modified Bessel 𝐾0 ) and inward avascular nests (convergent cylindrical geometry, modified Bessel 𝐼0 ). We derived an exact algebraic identity governing post-cessation exponential regrowth from molecular residual disease (ctDNA, 107 cells) to radiologic detection (CT, 109 cells). We evaluated the clinical prognostic relevance of histologic architecture in 604 resected lung adenocarcinoma patients from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC 2020). Results: In perivascular cords, outward radial diffusion of osimertinib (𝜆 = 627.6 𝜇m) produces a steep concentration drop beneath the IC50 threshold (𝜃 = 0.35, corresponding to unbound 𝐶0 ≈ 40 nM and IC50 ≈ 14 nM) at 𝑟crit = 165.9 𝜇m. Depending on physiological oxygenation limits, a viable pharmacological sanctuary shell of width Δ𝑟 = 34.1 𝜇m (for 𝑟ox = 200 𝜇m) or Δ𝑟 = 14.1 𝜇m (for 𝑟ox = 180 𝜇m) can persist. Under an assumed sigmoidal dose-response (ℎ = 1.5), residual drug exposure in the shell (𝐶 ≈ 0.31–0.35 𝐶0 ) maintains partial target inhibition (~45–50%), sufficient under physiological baseline apoptosis to induce near-zero net growth (cytostasis). Conversely, in inward avascular nests, convergent geometry maintains osimertinib at 90.6%–99.4% of boundary levels throughout viable regions (𝑅 ≤ 160–200 𝜇m), precluding small-molecule sanctuaries. For macromolecular antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs, 𝜆 = 77.5 𝜇m), central concentration drops below 𝜃 = 0.35 only for nest radii 𝑅 > 180 𝜇m, an architectural domain typically constrained by hypoxia and necrosis. In Monte Carlo parameter sampling (𝑁 = 10, 000 draws, log-normal priors, seed = 2), an outward perivascular sanctuary shell existed in 46.1% of parameter draws (62.8% when 𝑟ox = 200 𝜇m is fixed). The diagnostic lead time Δ𝑡 = 𝑇𝑠 ⋅ log2 (100) = 5.46 months (for doubling time 𝑇𝑠 = 25 days) is an analytical property of exponential expansion and assay thresholds, rather than an empirical confirmation of sanctuary existence. title: ROI-Guided Brain MRI Segmentation and Tumor-Region Visualization Using MATLAB
abstract: Abstract A MATLAB workflow and graphical user interface (GUI) are presented for region-of-interest (ROI)-guided segmentation and visualization of a suspected tumor region in brain magnetic resonance imaging. The method is applied to one axial FLAIR image from the REMBRANDT collection. A normalized 5 × 5 binomial kernel smooths the image. Central-difference filters provide a separate edge-magnitude view, while three fixed ROIs guide intensity-interval thresholding. A brightness cutoff and coordinate-based exclusions refine pixel selection. Binary hole filling is then applied to the mask used for the boundary overlay. The mathematical formulation defines each processing stage and its role in constructing the segmentation mask. The GUI displays the input, smoothed image, edge magnitude, isolated region, and boundary overlay in one window. These outputs show the selected region both in isolation and within the surrounding anatomy. The implementation brings image processing, visualization, and user interaction into a single MATLAB workflow.

title: Enhanced Breast Cancer Classification by Integrating CNN and ViT on the CBIS-DDSM Mammography Dataset
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, necessitating early and accurate diagnostic methods to improve patient outcomes. This study presents a novel hybrid approach for breast cancer classification by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures, specifically applied to the publicly available CBIS-DDSM mammography dataset. The initial phase employs a CNN model, which excels in localized feature extraction through convolutional layers, to identify key patterns related to benign and malignant tumors. However, CNNs inherently focus on local features and may overlook broader contextual relationships within the image. To overcome this limitation, the study introduces a hybrid framework that combines CNN with the Vision Transformer model. ViT utilizes self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies and global context, complementing the localized feature extraction capability of CNNs. By integrating these two deep learning paradigms, the hybrid model effectively captures both fine-grained local details and overarching structural patterns within mammograms. Experimental results indicate that synergy results in an improved classification accuracy. The enhanced performance of the combined CNN-ViT model underscores the potential of hybrid deep learning strategies in medical image analysis. Moreover, this approach demonstrates robust generalization on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, which includes diverse mammographic cases. The findings not only provide a pathway to more reliable breast cancer detection tools but also contribute to reducing diagnostic burden and improving early intervention strategies.

title: Intelligent System for Celiac Disease Detection Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Abstract In this study authors explore the application of deep learning techniques for the early detection of celiac disease through the analysis of medical imaging and clinical data. We used the convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed model exhibits promising accuracy in identifying patterns indicative of celiac disease from diverse images of a big database. The integration of deep learning in celiac disease diagnosis holds the potential for enhancing early intervention and improving patient outcomes, marking a significant advancement in medical diagnostics. The proposed approach elucidates the intricacies of celiac disease and implements a robust Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for accurate image classification. Achieving an average accuracy of 96%, this method promises enhanced diagnosis and management, paving the way for personalized healthcare interventions with significant improvements in patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: Multi-Task Framework for Efficient Knee Osteoarthritis Segmentation and Classification
abstract: Abstract Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a leading cause of chronic disability worldwide, and magnetic reso- nance imaging (MRI) remains the gold standard for assessing cartilage and meniscal integrity. While 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can leverage volumetric context for KOA analysis, they often incur high computational cost, increased memory demands, and susceptibility to learning from anatomically irrelevant regions. In this work, we propose a unified and flexible multi-task learning framework that accommodates both 2D slice-based and 3D volume-based convolutional backbones for joint KOA classification and knee structure segmentation. The architecture integrates a shared encoder configurable as either 2D or 3D followed by two task-specific branches: a dual-headed segmentation decoder for meniscus and cartilage masks, and a classification head operating on globally pooled features for KOA detection. We train and validate the framework on a large-scale dataset of 105,919 MRI slices, including expert-annotated segmentation masks and radiographically verified KOA labels. The multi-task design enables concurrent learning of anatomical and diagnostic signals at either the slice or volume level, improving task synergy and anatomical focus. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the 2D variant achieves more consistent segmentation quality, faster convergence, and lower computational overhead than a 3D VGG-UNet baseline while also delivering improved KOA classification accuracy.

title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Ovarian Cancer Subtype Classification Using Histopathology Images
abstract: Abstract Ovarian cancer is a histologically heterogeneous malignancy in which accurate subtype classification is essential for prognosis and treatment selection. Manual interpretation of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)–stained histopathology slides remains time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability, particularly for morphologically overlapping subtypes. In this study, an interpretable deep learning framework was developed for automated ovarian cancer subtype classification using a fine-tuned ResNet50 architecture. A publicly available histopathology dataset comprising five major ovarian carcinoma subtypes was employed. Model training incorporated optimized strategies including data augmentation, selective layer unfreezing, label smoothing, and test-time augmentation. Classification performance was benchmarked against established convolutional neural network architectures. Visual interpretability was assessed using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to examine model attention patterns. The proposed framework achieved high classification performance, with strong accuracy and macro-averaged F1-scores across subtypes. Grad-CAM analysis demonstrated that model attention was consistently localized to histologically relevant tissue regions in correctly classified samples, while misclassifications were associated with morphologically ambiguous structures. These findings suggest that classification errors primarily reflect intrinsic histopathologic overlap rather than spurious model behavior. Overall, this work establishes a reproducible and interpretable deep learning benchmark for ovarian cancer subtype classification and provides clinically meaningful insight into model decision processes. The proposed framework is well-suited for use as a second-reader decision support tool in digital pathology workflows.

title: Joint Classification and Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning for Cervical Cancer Detection in Histopathological Images
abstract: Abstract Correct categorization of histopathological images of the cervix is very crucial if one is to identify and treat any emerging cases of cervical cancer on time. However, this is not an easy task, given that there is so much variability within one class while there are only minute distinctions between normal and pathological tissues. In our study, we therefore develop a deep learning approach that combines contrast learning with the traditional approach of using the cross-entropy loss function to correctly categorize histopathological images of the cervix into normal or pathological tissues. Our approach is based on ResNet-50 and seeks to maximize both learning of appropriate features and correct classification of images into one of two classes: normal or pathological cervical tissues. Performance is evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation on a variety of metrics, including balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, as well as average precision. For the histopathological dataset, CAISHI, this approach in all cases produces very high balanced accuracy of 96.90 ± 0.23 on average. High precision, recall, and F1 values indicate a high accuracy of abnormal region detection. In comparison to existing machine learning techniques, CNN models, transformer networks, and a few-shot learning strategy, the proposed approach demonstrates improved robustness and generalization capabilities. From the results, it can be inferred that the integration of supervised contrastive learning with deep convolutional feature extraction leads to a dramatic improvement in the representation ability and classification accuracy in the field of cervical histopathology images. The proposed framework can indeed be used as a robust interpretation solution with high potential for medical support in cervical cancer diagnosis.

title: QSGT: Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer for Faithful Multi-modal Radiology Report Summarization
abstract: Abstract Improving the alignment between visual evidence andtextual descriptions in medical vision-language models(VLM) remains a critical challenge for achieving entitylevelfaithfulness in low-resource generation tasks. Thispaper proposes Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer(QSGT), a hybrid approach of token pruningand mixture of experts (MoE), grounded on the conceptionof quantum many-body wavefunction. This hybridapproach was aimed at improving the selectionof both modality-specific expert tokens and the formationof non-dominating experts to determine stableconjugates. The token pruning approach was improvedusing the quantum orbital style token assignments andthe mixture of experts by the quantum doubly occupancyapproximation. We also introduce two clinicallymotivated regularization terms, pair loss and seniorityloss, further enforce semantic consistency and dominanceof diagnostically relevant features. Our extensiveexperiments across seven thoracic disease categoriesdemonstrate that QSGT significantly outperforms stateof-the-art medical VLMs on multiple evaluation metrics,including RadGraph (36.2), SPICE (42.68), andconsistently high BERTScore (98), on the MIMIC-CXRtest set. QSGT achieves substantial gains in clinical correctnessand semantic accuracy, particularly for complexconditions such as pneumonia and pneumothorax. Ablationstudies confirmthe importance of each architecturalcomponent, while convergence analyses show stable andinterpretable learning dynamics. These results indicate that QSGT provides a robust and clinically meaningfulsolution for multimodal medical report summarization,enabling more reliable, interpretable, and patientcentredclinical AI systems.

title: Resistance to thyroid hormone β (RTHβ) due to a THRB mutation (p.Arg429Gln) in a39-year-old woman initially treated for thyrotoxicosis
abstract: Abstract Background Resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ) is a rare inherited disorder characterised by elevated free thyroid hormone levels with non-suppressed or elevated TSH, most commonly caused by mutations in the THRB gene. The biochemical profile often mimics thyrotoxicosis or a TSH secreting pituitary adenoma, contributing to delayed or inappropriate treatment. Methods We describe the clinical course, biochemical findings and genetic analysis of a 39 year old woman who presented with palpitations, hypertension and elevated FT4 and FT3 despite a non-suppressed TSH, and who demonstrated no response to antithyroid medication. Genetic sequencing was performed. Results Initial testing showed normal TSH levels (2.45 mU/L), and elevated FT4 (29 pmol/L) and FT3 (7.6 pmol/L). Antithyroid therapy (Thiamazole) led to a paradoxal rise in TSH. Pituitary MRI was normal. Genetic analysis identified a heterozygous THRB gene variant, NM_001354712.2:c.1286G>A (p.Arg429Gln), classified as pathogenic. Antithyroid therapy was discontinued, and management was transitioned to betablockade. The patient remained clinically stable at a 24-months follow-up, and genetic counselling was initiated. Conclusion This case highlights that elevated FT4/FT3 with inappropriately normal or high TSH should raise suspicion of RTHβ. Genetic confirmation is critical to avoid unnecessary interventions and to guide appropriate long-term management and family screening.

title: Deep learning-assisted target volume segmentation for uterine malignancies on non-contrast CT
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate delineation of clinical target volume (CTV) and planning target volume (PTV) is essential for radiotherapy in uterine malignancies. However, the limited soft-tissue contrast of non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) makes automated target segmentation challenging. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 157 unique patients. Of these, 137 patients were used for model development and internal testing, including a development cohort of 110 patients and an independent test cohort of 27 patients. A separate cohort of 20 patients was used for workflow evaluation. A multi-label nnU-Net model was developed to simultaneously segment the CTV and PTV. Four nnU-Net configurations were compared using five-fold cross-validation. Segmentation performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). Three radiation oncologists independently assessed the clinical acceptability of the auto-contours using a four-point Likert scale. Workflow efficiency was evaluated by comparing manual contouring with AI-assisted contour editing. Results: The 3D-fullres configuration achieved the numerically highest overall cross-validation performance and was selected for independent internal testing. In the 27-patient independent test cohort, the mean DSC was 90.02% ± 2.33% for PTV and 72.16% ± 4.54% for CTV. The corresponding median HD95 values were 5.12 mm (interquartile range [IQR], 5.00–7.60 mm) and 5.55 mm (IQR, 5.00–9.50 mm), respectively. Rating-level clinical acceptability was 91.4% for PTV and 75.3% for CTV. Inter-rater agreement was higher for PTV than for CTV. In the separate workflow cohort, AI-assisted contouring reduced the mean total task time from 65.4 to 14.2 minutes per case, corresponding to an observed reduction of 78.3% (P<0.001). Conclusion: The multi-label 3D-fullres nnU-Net achieved high PTV overlap and moderate CTV overlap on internal NCCT data and reduced contouring time in a separate workflow cohort. The model may provide editable initial contours, but CTV predictions require careful physician review. External validation and dosimetric assessment are required before routine clinical use.

title: Energy-Based Devices for GLP-1 Receptor Agonist-Associated Facial Aging: A Tissue-Specific Safety Framework.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA)-associated rapid weight loss may be accompanied by facial changes resembling accelerated aging, colloquially termed "Ozempic face". In this review, this proposed phenotype is termed GLP-1RA-associated facial accelerated aging (GLP-1RA-FAA) and is characterized primarily by facial volume loss and skin laxity, with possible but incompletely characterized alterations in dermal-adipose support, adipose-derived stem-cell biology, fibroblast-extracellular-matrix homeostasis, and facial muscle. Demand for energy-based device (EBD) treatment in this population is increasing; however, whether conventional EBD parameters are effective or safe in medication-associated facial volume depletion is unknown. A narrative review was informed by structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 through August 31, 2026. Evidence was selected for clinical directness and relevance to radiofrequency, high-intensity focused ultrasound, broadband light, microwave, extracorporeal shock wave therapy, diode laser, and synchronized radiofrequency with high-intensity facial electrical stimulation. Available modalities differ in their intended tissue depth and in the potential relevance of three conceptual targets: preservation of adipose tissue, dermal fibroblast-extracellular-matrix remodeling, and facial muscle-SMAS support. Preclinical body-contouring studies suggest that sustained subcutaneous heating in the approximate 43-45°C range can be associated with adipocyte injury or apoptosis; however, no facial thermal dose threshold has been established, particularly in GLP-1RA-treated patients. No individual EBD modality has demonstrated simultaneous restoration of adipose, dermal, and muscle-related targets in prospective GLP-1RA-specific studies. Conservative control of treatment depth, careful avoidance of unnecessary deep energy deposition in volume-depleted regions, investigation of low-intensity dermal remodeling strategies, and evaluation of muscle-targeting approaches are proposed as research considerations. These concepts are hypothesis generating and do not constitute clinical recommendations or standards of care. Prospective controlled studies in well-characterized GLP-1RA-treated populations are required before device-specific protocols can be adopted.

title: Localized Bullous Pemphigoid of the Scalp and Face with Suspected Vulvar Involvement: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Localized bullous pemphigoid (LBP) is a form of bullous pemphigoid (BP) confined to a limited anatomical area. Classification becomes less certain when clinically similar lesions occur at a distant site without site-specific immunopathologic confirmation. We report immunopathologically supported scalp/facial BP-spectrum disease with a temporally associated but unconfirmed vulvar eruption. Case presentation A 51-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of pruritic erythema and tense bullae on the scalp and face and a 1-month history of erythematous scaly plaques with hemorrhagic bullous lesions in the vulvar region. Scalp histopathology showed a subepidermal blister with eosinophil-rich inflammation, and direct immunofluorescence (DIF) of perilesional scalp skin showed linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone. Infectious studies of the vulvar eruption were negative. Anti-BP180/230 serology, indirect immunofluorescence, salt-split skin studies, and anti-type VII collagen antibody testing were unavailable. Vulvar biopsy and DIF were not performed; therefore, vulvar BP could not be confirmed. With systemic and topical corticosteroids plus adjunctive minocycline, no new bullae developed by day 5, and the lesions markedly improved within 2 weeks. Methylprednisolone was subsequently tapered from 40 mg/day to a maintenance dose of 4 mg/day; minocycline and topical corticosteroids were discontinued after sustained clinical improvement. At 6 months, the disease remained clinically controlled on methylprednisolone 4 mg/day, with no new bullae or clinically evident recurrence. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Conclusion The findings support localized BP/BP-spectrum disease of the scalp and face, while the vulvar eruption remains unconfirmed. The parallel treatment response is supportive but not diagnostic of vulvar BP. When feasible, lesions at sensitive sites should undergo site-specific biopsy and DIF. If biopsy is declined or impractical, pretreatment morphology should be carefully documented, diagnostic uncertainty should be acknowledged, and follow-up should assess for scarring and additional mucosal involvement.

title: Advances in the LI-RADS Treatment Response Algorithm: Imaging Principles, Diagnostic Challenges, and Clinical Integration Following the LI-RADS 2024 Update.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) management has evolved rapidly with the expanding use of locoregional therapies, systemic agents, and modern immunotherapy combinations. These advances have introduced complex and variable post-treatment imaging appearances, underscoring the need for refined, standardized criteria to accurately differentiate viable tumors from treatment-related changes. The updated LI-RADS Treatment Response Algorithm (v2024-2025) incorporates new guidance on arterial enhancement, washout, ancillary features, and modality-specific considerations to improve consistency and diagnostic clarity. This review synthesizes these updates and their implications for clinical practice. A comprehensive narrative review was conducted using updated LI-RADS guidelines and recent literature evaluating CT, MRI, CEUS, dual-energy CT, and photon-counting CT for post-treatment HCC assessment. Therapy-specific imaging appearances, algorithmic refinements, pitfalls, radiologic-pathologic correlations, and applications of artificial intelligence were analyzed. The updated LI-RADS TRA has shown potential lesion-level assessment by clarifying criteria for viable, non-viable, and equivocal responses. Multiparametric MRI and spectral CT improve the detection of subtle viable tissue, while advanced imaging helps address confounding factors such as granulation tissue, perfusional changes, and immune-related pseudo-progression. The algorithm demonstrates high accuracy after ablation and TACE, with ongoing refinements needed for radiotherapy and immunotherapy. Radiomics and machine learning models show strong potential for automated viability assessment and early prediction of recurrence. The LI-RADS TRA (v2024-2025) strengthens standardization of post-treatment HCC imaging and supports more accurate, reproducible interpretation across modalities. As treatment options expand, integrating quantitative imaging biomarkers and AI-driven tools will be essential for personalized treatment planning and improved clinical outcomes.

title: Scleroderma-Like Skin Changes and Multifocal Muscle Thickening in a Patient with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Paraneoplastic rheumatic manifestations may precede the diagnosis of an occult malignancy and closely mimic primary autoimmune connective-tissue diseases. Scleroderma-like manifestations have rarely been reported in association with lymphoid malignancies, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Case presentation A 47-year-old woman presented with progressive skin thickening, difficulty walking, reduced appetite, and weight loss. She had been diagnosed with scleroderma by an outside physician in early 2024 and had been treated with methotrexate 15 mg once weekly. Physical examination revealed facial skin tightening, sclerodactyly, skin induration extending to the wrists and elbows, and asymmetric thickening of the right neck, forearm, and thigh muscles. Pruritic migratory annular plaques were observed on the trunk and resolved spontaneously within two weeks, clinically suggesting an erythema annulare centrifugum-like eruption. Raynaud phenomenon was absent, antinuclear antibody testing was negative, and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy was present. Computed tomography demonstrated multiple destructive osteolytic lesions in the lumbar vertebrae. Neck magnetic resonance imaging showed edema-like T2 hyperintensity involving the sternocleidomastoid muscle and adjacent tissues without contrast enhancement. Biopsy of a vertebral lesion revealed DLBCL, with tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen and CD20 and a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80%. The patient was started on standard first-line R-CHOP immunochemotherapy but died in the intensive care unit after the first treatment administration, precluding assessment of treatment response and longer-term follow-up. Conclusion This case illustrates an unusual presentation of DLBCL accompanied by scleroderma-like cutaneous changes, multifocal muscle thickening, and an annular eruption. The simultaneous absence of Raynaud phenomenon and antinuclear antibodies, together with constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, asymmetric soft-tissue abnormalities, and destructive bone lesions, should prompt reconsideration of presumed systemic sclerosis and evaluation for an underlying malignancy. Although a paraneoplastic association was strongly suspected, it could not be confirmed because the patient died after the first treatment administration, precluding assessment of the rheumatic manifestations after lymphoma-directed therapy.

title: Comparisons in Analgesic Effects Between Ultrasound-Guided Erector Spinae Plane Block and Ultrasound-Guided Modified Intercostal Nerve Block in Modified Radical Mastectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Introduction Postoperative acute pain is a common challenge after breast cancer surgery. This randomized controlled trial compared the analgesic effects of ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and modified intercostal nerve block (MINB) in patients undergoing unilateral modified radical mastectomy. Methods Seventy patients were randomly allocated to ESPB or MINB group. The primary outcomes were the 6-hour postoperative resting and movement-evoked Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores. Secondary outcomes included resting and movement-evoked VAS scores at 0, 3, 12, and 24 hours, intraoperative opioid consumption, rescue analgesic use within 72 hours, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 hours, and hospital stay. Results At 6 hours postoperatively, both resting VAS (median 2 [0-2] vs 2 [2-3], P=0.005) and movement-evoked VAS (median 3 [2-4] vs 4 [3-4], P=0.015) were lower in the MINB group. Resting VAS scores at 0 and 3 hours were comparable between groups. Movement-evoked VAS scores were lower in the MINB group at all post-surgery time points (P<0.05 for all). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was lower in the MINB group (P<0.001). Fewer patients required rescue analgesics in the MINB group (P=0.038). No significant difference was observed in QoR-15 scores between groups (P=0.055). Conclusion Ultrasound-guided MINB was associated with lower 6-hour resting and movement-evoked pain scores and reduced intraoperative opioid consumption compared with ESPB, without compromising recovery quality in patients undergoing unilateral modified radical mastectomy. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300077956; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.aspx?proj=77956). Registered on November 24, 2023. Principal investigator: Guanghong Xu.

title: Liposomal Bupivacaine Combined with Bupivacaine vs Ropivacaine for Paravertebral Blockade in Single-Port Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Propensity-Matched Comparison of Postoperative Opioid Use.
abstract: Objective To compare the effect of preoperative single-injection paravertebral block using liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine mixture versus ropivacaine on cumulative postoperative opioid consumption in patients undergoing thoracic surgery. Methods This retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (wedge resection, segmentectomy, or lobectomy) between January 2024 and February 2026. Patients received an ultrasound-guided single-injection paravertebral block with either 0.5% ropivacaine (20 mL) or a mixture of 1.3% liposomal bupivacaine (10 mL) and 0.5% standard bupivacaine (10 mL). The primary outcome was cumulative postoperative opioid consumption throughout the hospitalization, delivered via patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) and converted to oral morphine milligram equivalents. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, time to first PCA request, postoperative adverse events, and length of stay. Propensity score matching (1:2) was performed to balance baseline clinical and intraoperative characteristics. Results Among 492 eligible patients, 331 received ropivacaine and 161 received liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine combination. After matching, 210 and 108 patients were included in the ropivacaine and liposomal bupivacaine groups, respectively. The median cumulative postoperative opioid consumption was lower in the liposomal bupivacaine group (92.1 mg [IQR, 59.1-122.3]) than in the ropivacaine group (226.2 mg [IQR, 170.2-260.0]), with a median difference of 128.2 mg (95% CI, 111.0-143.9; P < 0.001). The liposomal bupivacaine group was also associated with lower resting and movement pain scores at 24 and 48 hours postoperatively, a longer time to first PCA press (26.0 vs. 6.0 hours; P < 0.001), and a lower incidence of postoperative dizziness (21.3% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.017). Conclusion For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, preoperative single-injection paravertebral blockade with liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine mixture was associated with lower cumulative postoperative opioid consumption and lower early postoperative pain scores than ropivacaine.

title: <sup>68</sup>Ga/<sup>177</sup>Lu-Labeled Seribantumab as the Theranostic Drugs in Treating HER3-Positive Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major clinical challenge due to its high recurrence rate, poor response to systemic therapies, and unfavorable prognosis. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) has emerged as a clinically relevant molecular target in HCC. Seribantumab is a fully human IgG2 monoclonal antibody against HER3 and can inhibit downstream pro-survival signaling and exert potential antitumor effects. This study aimed to develop Seribantumab-based HER3-targeted radionuclide drug conjugates ( 68 Ga/ 177 Lu-Seribantumab) for HER3-targeted imaging and radionuclide therapy of HCC. Methods Seribantumab was conjugated with isothiocyanate-benzyl-DOTA and radiolabeled with 68 Ga or 177 Lu. 177 Lu-Seribantumab was evaluated for radiochemical purity, stability, cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, cell-cycle distribution, DNA damage, and apoptosis. PET/CT imaging, biodistribution, therapeutic efficacy, and histology were assessed in HepG2 xenograft mice treated with 68 Ga/ 177 Lu-Seribantumab. Results Both 68 Ga-Seribantumab and 177 Lu-Seribantumab exhibited high radiochemical purity (>95%) and stability. 177 Lu-Seribantumab showed HER3-specific cellular uptake and cytotoxic effects in HepG2 cells. 177 Lu-Seribantumab induced G1-phase cell-cycle arrest and enhanced DNA damage and apoptosis (29.1 ± 2.1%) in HepG2 cells, consistent with HER3-targeted effects accompanied by radionuclide-associated cytotoxicity. Similar cell-cycle and apoptotic effects were observed in Huh7 cells. Furthermore, PET/CT showed partly HER3-mediated tumor uptake of 68 Ga-Seribantumab, although the tumor-to-liver contrast was modest. SPECT/CT imaging further demonstrated sustained tumor accumulation of 177 Lu-Seribantumab in HepG2 xenografts, reaching 1.1 ± 0.1%ID/mL at 24 h, thereby supporting its tumor-targeting capability and therapeutic potential. Histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses revealed extensive tumor necrosis, increased Caspase-3 expression, reduced Ki67 positivity, and decreased HER3-positive tumor cell populations after treatment with radionuclide drug conjugates (RDCs), further supporting the antitumor activity of 177 Lu-Seribantumab. Conclusion 68 Ga/ 177 Lu-conjugated Seribantumab enables HER3-targeted molecular imaging and radionuclide therapy in HER3-positive HCC models. These findings support the potential of Seribantumab-based RDCs as a theranostic strategy for HER3-positive HCC.

title: Added Prognostic Value of MRI to CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy in the Extended Time Window.
abstract: Background In the 6-24-hour window, imaging must identify patients with salvageable tissue while avoiding delays and reperfusion of large established infarcts. The optimal imaging strategy remains controversial. Although computed tomography (CT) is widely used because of its accessibility and speed, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides more sensitive tissue characterization. This study evaluated whether adding MRI to CT was associated with clinical outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT). Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of consecutive patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion who underwent MT between January 2022 and December 2024. Patients were grouped according to pre-procedural imaging: CT alone or MRI plus CT. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to reduce measured baseline imbalances. The primary outcomes were excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1) and 3-month mortality; symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (SICH) was the secondary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations. Results After propensity score matching, 364 patients (182 pairs) were included in the final analysis. Compared with CT alone, the MRI plus CT group demonstrated significantly lower 3-month mortality (7.1% vs 18.7%, P < 0.01) and reduced incidence of SICH (2.2% vs 7.7%, P = 0.02). No significant difference was observed in excellent functional outcome at 3 months between groups. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that MRI plus CT was independently associated with lower risks of mortality (adjusted OR=0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.72; P < 0.01) and SICH (adjusted OR=0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.96; P =0.04). Conclusion Among patients with AIS undergoing MT within the 6-24-hour window, MRI plus CT was associated with lower 3-month mortality and SICH than CT alone, without a significant difference in excellent functional outcome. Because imaging allocation was non-randomized and quantitative infarct-core and perfusion data were unavailable, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require prospective multicenter validation.

Patients were grouped according to pre-procedural imaging: CT alone or MRI plus CT. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to reduce measured baseline imbalances. The primary outcomes were excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1) and 3-month mortality; symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (SICH) was the secondary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations.

Results

After propensity score matching, 364 patients (182 pairs) were included in the final analysis. Compared with CT alone, the MRI plus CT group demonstrated significantly lower 3-month mortality (7.1% vs 18.7%, P < 0.01) and reduced incidence of SICH (2.2% vs 7.7%, P = 0.02). No significant difference was observed in excellent functional outcome at 3 months between groups. Conclusion

Among patients with AIS undergoing MT within the 6-24-hour window, MRI plus CT was associated with lower 3-month mortality and SICH than CT alone, without a significant difference in excellent functional outcome. title: MRI-Based Intratumoral and Multi-Range Peritumoral Radiomics for Predicting Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer.
abstract: Background To determine the best-performing peritumoral boundary among tested distances and evaluate the predictive value of preoperative multiparametric MRI radiomics for axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) in breast cancer. Methods Clinical and imaging data of 273 patients from two centers were retrospectively analyzed. ROIs were manually delineated on Fs-T2WI and DCE-MRI images, and peritumoral regions were generated by expanding the tumor ROI by 3 mm, 5 mm, and 7 mm. Patients from Center 1 (n = 201) were randomly divided into training and internal validation set (7:3), while Center 2 (n = 72) served as the external validation set. LASSO regression and an SVM classifier were used to construct predictive models. A nomogram integrating the best-performing radiomic model with clinical parameters was developed. Model performance was assessed using AUC and DCA. Results Maximum tumor diameter was identified as an independent risk factor for ALNM (OR = 4.042, 95% CI: 2.488-6.532; P < 0.001). Among the tested peritumoral margins, the 5 mm model demonstrated the best predictive efficacy, significantly outperforming both 3 mm (AUC 0.694) and 7 mm (AUC 0.717) models (DeLong test, all P < 0.05). The fusion model combining DCE-MRI intra- and peritumoral (5 mm) features with Fs-T2WI intratumoral features achieved AUCs of 0.909, 0.818, and 0.768 in the training, internal validation, and external validation sets, respectively. The nomogram integrating the fusion model with maximum tumor diameter further improved performance, with AUCs of 0.943, 0.884, and 0.853, respectively. Conclusion Among the tested distances, a 5 mm peritumoral margin provided the best predictive performance for ALNM. The multiparametric MRI radiomic model effectively predicts ALNM and offers a valuable non-invasive tool for preoperative assessment.

title: Evaluation of PDA‑PLL Nanoparticles for siRNA Delivery and ROS Scavenging in Rat Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Introduction Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent chronic inflammatory disease in which elevated TNF-α and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) play central roles. These two pathological factors mutually reinforce each other-TNF-α induces ROS production while ROS upregulates TNF-α expression-forming a vicious cycle that propels disease progression. However, current therapies offer only symptomatic relief without halting this process. To address this, we developed polydopamine-poly(L-lysine) (PDA-PLL) nanoparticles as a dual-functional platform that combines PDA-mediated ROS scavenging with PLL-facilitated TNF-α siRNA delivery. Methods PDA-PLL nanoparticles were synthesized and systematically characterized, and then their gene transfection efficiency and ROS scavenging capacity were evaluated. Finally, their therapeutic efficacy against OA was assessed in chondrocytes and in animal models. Results Biocompatibility was evidenced by low in-vitro cytotoxicity and the absence of systemic toxicity in rats by hematology, biochemistry, and histopathology. Agarose gel electrophoresis demonstrated their strong nucleic acid loading capability, and fluorescence imaging further revealed that PDA-PLL nanoparticles enabled highly efficient gene transfection in OA chondrocytes. PDA-PLL nanoparticles exhibited dose-dependent scavenging of O 2 •-, • OH, and H 2 O 2 in cell-free assays and lowered intracellular ROS in OA chondrocytes; critically, co-delivery of TNF-α siRNA further reduced ROS versus PDA-PLL alone. Consistent with these findings, the PDA-PLL+TNF-α siRNA group showed stronger suppression of inflammatory genes, greater restoration of matrix-preserving genes, and enhanced cytoprotection compared with PDA-PLL alone. In rat OA, PDA-PLL+siRNA outperformed PDA-PLL alone, with macroscopic and histological outcomes approaching the sham group. Conclusion This work presents PDA-PLL nanoparticles as a multifunctional therapeutic system that unites efficient gene delivery with potent ROS scavenging. Their synergistic action resulted in significant protection of chondrocytes and potent therapeutic efficacy in OA models.

title: CXCL10-Targeted Nanoparticle Enables Ultrasound Molecular Imaging of Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy-Induced Immune Remodeling in Rectal Cancer.
abstract: Purpose Rectal cancer patients show significant heterogeneity in their response to neoadjuvant therapy, which stems from the differential remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment caused by chemoradiotherapy. Currently, there is a lack of monitoring methods to capture this immune activation signal early in clinical practice. To address this, we developed liquid-gas phase change lipid nanoparticles targeting CXCL10 for non-invasive ultrasound molecular imaging to monitor tumor immune responses during neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Methods We analyzed the expression of CXCL10 in colorectal cancer tissues and its correlation with patient prognosis, as well as CXCL10's ability of chemotactism to T cells. We constructed phase-change lipid nanoparticles modified with CXCL10 antibodies (aCXCL10/PFP@Lipid), and systematically assessed in vitro physicochemical properties, antibody modification, cell uptake, and phase transformation efficiency. In mouse rectal cancer models, we evaluated biosafety, biodistribution, ultrasound imaging, and chemoradiotherapy efficacy, followed by testing the immune microenvironment of tumor tissues. Results CXCL10 was highly expressed in macrophages and a distinct subset of tumor‑enriched endothelial cells, and the abundance of this endothelial subset correlated significantly with favorable prognosis. The CXCL10-CXCR3 signaling axis was a key pathway mediating the chemotactic migration of CD8⁺ T cells. The aCXCL10/PFP@Lipid nanoparticles exhibited uniform size (62.97 ± 0.83 nm) and excellent tumor targeting. Upon low-intensity pulsed ultrasound irradiation, nanoparticles underwent phase transition to microbubbles, producing markedly increased contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) signals. After chemoradiotherapy, the treatment group showed an increase in CXCL10 expression levels, as well as the CEUS signals. Compared to the untreated control group, the tumor suppression rate reached 89.45%, with an increasing expression of CD4⁺, CD8⁺, CD3 + and CD68⁺ in tumor tissue, while decreased Foxp3. Conclusion The aCXCL10/PFP@Lipid enables effective ultrasound molecular visualization of CXCL10 expression, offering a potential novel noninvasive strategy for monitoring of the tumor immune microenvironment and treatment response in colorectal cancer.

title: Staged Management of Recurrent Obstructed Hemivagina in Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich Syndrome: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Background Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS) is a rare congenital Müllerian anomaly characterized by uterus didelphys, obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal anomaly. Recurrence after prior surgical treatment is particularly rare. We report a complex recurrent case of obstructed hemivagina in a patient with HWWS and duplicated vagina, successfully managed with a staged surgical approach. Case presentation A 19-year-old woman with a history of two prior vaginal septum resections and excision of a perineal mass (histopathology confirming ectopic colonic tissue) presented with recurrent pelvic pain and fever. MRI and endoscopic assessment demonstrated uterus didelphys, duplicated cervices and vaginas, complete obstruction of the right hemivagina, ipsilateral renal agenesis, and a deeply recessed obstructed cavity containing purulent fluid. Because of the markedly distorted postoperative anatomy, a staged surgical strategy was adopted. The first stage involved hysteroscopic and vaginoscopic decompression with ultrasound-guided septal incision and drainage. The second stage consisted of definitive reconstruction, including resection of the accessory blind tract, obliteration of the residual obstructed cavity, and perineal reconstruction. The patient recovered uneventfully, resumed regular painless menstruation. No recurrence of hemivaginal obstruction was observed during follow-up.However, the diagnosis was not definitive. The patient had lifelong persistent urinary incontinence that showed no improvement after surgery. Although a right ectopic ureter or ureterocele was unlikely to account for the continuous leakage because the right kidney was nonfunctioning, a left ectopic ureter and other lower urinary tract abnormalities had not been fully excluded. Conclusions This case highlights a complex recurrent presentation of HWWS and emphasizes the importance of MRI and endoscopic evaluation in delineating atypical postoperative anatomy. Individualized staged surgical management may help prevent re-obstruction, control infection, restore functional genital tract continuity, and preserve future reproductive potential in patients with complicated or recurrent HWWS. Persistent urinary incontinence and a history of perineal ectopic colonic tissue warrant further urological and multidisciplinary evaluation, a left ectopic ureter and other lower urinary tract abnormalities should be carefully evaluated in this patients.

title: A Case Report of a Giant Mucinous Cystadenoma Suspected to Be Associated with Ovarian Remnant Syndrome After Bilateral Adnexectomy: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Implications for Clinical Management.
abstract: Background Mucinous cystadenoma of the ovary is one of the common benign ovarian neoplasms. Nevertheless, when a huge pelvic mass develops years after bilateral adnexectomy, determining its tissue origin and establishing a differential diagnosis poses substantial challenges, complicating the clinical management of such secondary pelvic lesions. Case presentation This study reports a rare case of a giant pelvic mass occurring many years after bilateral adnexectomy in a 65-year-old Han Chinese female. Intraoperative exploration and postoperative histopathology confirmed the lesion as an ovarian mucinous cystadenoma, which was presumed to arise from residual ovarian tissue after previous surgery, consistent with ovarian remnant syndrome (ORS). However, the ovarian origin of this lesion was comprehensively determined based on prior surgical records, intraoperative findings, and histopathological morphology, without further confirmation by definitive immunohistochemical staining. Conclusion Ovarian remnant syndrome should be considered in the differential diagnosis of de novo pelvic masses following bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. A review of prior surgical records is essential for tracing the origin of such lesions. For pelvic mucinous lesions, gastrointestinal and appendiceal origins should be prioritized for exclusion, accompanied by comprehensive characterization of pathological features. To minimize the risk of long-term postoperative lesions, complete resection of all ovarian tissue should be pursued during bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in routine clinical practice.
